### Pattern 124: Playwright per-worker authentication with `parallelIndex` — deterministic DB user slots for parallel tests (TypeScript, Playwright 1.40+)

When tests run in parallel and each test needs an authenticated user with unique server-side state, the `parallelIndex` fixture provides a stable worker slot number that survives retries without colliding.

```typescript
// tests/fixtures/auth.fixture.ts
import { test as base, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';
import { createTestUser, deleteTestUser } from '../helpers/db.js';

interface AuthFixtures {
  authenticatedContext: BrowserContext;
  testUserId: string;
}

export const test = base.extend<{}, AuthFixtures>({
  // Worker-scoped: one user per parallel slot across all tests in the worker
  testUserId: [
    async ({ parallelIndex }, use) => {
      // parallelIndex is STABLE across retries — workerIndex is NOT
      const userId = `test-worker-${parallelIndex}`;
      await createTestUser(userId, { email: `worker${parallelIndex}@test.example` });

      await use(userId);

      // Teardown: runs once when the worker exits
      await deleteTestUser(userId);
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],

  authenticatedContext: [
    async ({ browser, testUserId }, use) => {
      // Per-worker context reused for all tests — login state persists across tests in worker
      const storageStatePath = `playwright/.auth/worker-${testUserId}.json`;
      const context = await browser.newContext({ storageState: storageStatePath });
      await use(context);
      await context.close();
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

// tests/profile.test.ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { test } from './fixtures/auth.fixture.js';

test('can view own profile', async ({ authenticatedContext }) => {
  const page = await authenticatedContext.newPage();
  await page.goto('/profile');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /profile/i })).toBeVisible();
  await page.close();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Worker-scoped fixtures are initialized once per worker and shared across all tests in that worker. A test that mutates the authenticated user's profile (e.g., changes email) will corrupt subsequent tests in the same worker. Use `scope: 'test'` and `storageState` cloning if tests modify user state; use `scope: 'worker'` only for read-heavy test suites. [official]

---

### Pattern 125: Jest `jest.useFakeTimers({ doNotFake })` — selective timer isolation for tests using `performance.now` or real `Date` (TypeScript, Jest 27+)

`jest.useFakeTimers()` replaces `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `performance`, and other globals by default. When code under test intentionally uses `performance.now()` for benchmarking, faking it breaks the semantics. `doNotFake` opts specific APIs out.

```typescript
// src/rate-limiter.ts
export class RateLimiter {
  private calls: number[] = [];
  constructor(private readonly maxCallsPerWindow: number, private readonly windowMs: number) {}

  isAllowed(): boolean {
    const now = Date.now();
    this.calls = this.calls.filter((t) => now - t < this.windowMs);
    if (this.calls.length >= this.maxCallsPerWindow) return false;
    this.calls.push(now);
    return true;
  }
}

// tests/rate-limiter.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { RateLimiter } from '../src/rate-limiter.js';

describe('RateLimiter', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    jest.useFakeTimers({
      // Fake Date and setTimeout — but keep performance real
      doNotFake: ['performance'],
      now: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z').getTime(),
    });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    jest.useRealTimers(); // always restore — prevents timer state leaking to next test
  });

  it('allows calls within the limit', () => {
    const limiter = new RateLimiter(3, 1000);
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(true);
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(true);
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(true);
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(false); // 4th call blocked
  });

  it('resets after window advances', () => {
    const limiter = new RateLimiter(2, 1000);
    limiter.isAllowed();
    limiter.isAllowed();
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(false);

    // Advance fake clock by 1100ms — calls fall outside window
    jest.advanceTimersByTime(1100);
    expect(limiter.isAllowed()).toBe(true);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `doNotFake` requires listing APIs by their exact property names as strings (e.g., `'performance'`, `'queueMicrotask'`). Forgetting `afterEach(() => jest.useRealTimers())` leaks fake timers into subsequent test files in the same worker — a famously hard-to-diagnose issue. Always pair `useFakeTimers` with `useRealTimers` in the matching teardown hook, OR set `fakeTimers: { ... }` at the Jest config level to auto-apply project-wide with no per-test setup/teardown needed. [official]

---

### Pattern 126: Vitest `sequence.hooks: 'stack'` model — ensuring setup/teardown symmetry in nested describe blocks (TypeScript, Vitest 4.0+)

Vitest 4.0 introduced `sequence.hooks` to control whether lifecycle hooks run in stack order (LIFO for teardown) or in the order they were registered. The stack model (the new default) guarantees that an `afterAll` registered after `beforeAll` tears down in reverse order — matching the mental model of a call stack.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    sequence: {
      // 'stack' (default in Vitest 4.0+): afterEach/afterAll run in REVERSE registration order
      // 'list' (pre-4.0 default): run in registration order
      hooks: 'stack',
    },
  },
});
```

```typescript
// tests/multi-layer-teardown.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterAll } from 'vitest';

const teardownOrder: string[] = [];

describe('Outer suite', () => {
  beforeAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('outer-setup'); });
  afterAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('outer-teardown'); }); // runs LAST

  describe('Inner suite A', () => {
    beforeAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('inner-A-setup'); });
    afterAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('inner-A-teardown'); });

    it('runs', () => expect(true).toBe(true));
  });

  describe('Inner suite B', () => {
    beforeAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('inner-B-setup'); });
    afterAll(() => { teardownOrder.push('inner-B-teardown'); });

    it('also runs', () => expect(true).toBe(true));
  });

  // With sequence.hooks: 'stack', teardown order is:
  // inner-B-teardown → inner-A-teardown → outer-teardown
  // This mirrors the setup call stack in reverse — database connections
  // opened last are closed first, preventing use-after-free errors.
  it('verifies setup ordering captured so far', () => {
    expect(teardownOrder).toEqual([
      'outer-setup',
      'inner-A-setup',
      'inner-A-teardown',
      'inner-B-setup',
      'inner-B-teardown',
    ]);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Switching from `'list'` to `'stack'` in an existing codebase can silently reverse teardown order for suites that previously relied on the `'list'` behaviour — specifically any suite where one `afterAll` depends on a resource released by a subsequent `afterAll`. Audit nested `afterAll` chains before upgrading. The `'stack'` model is strongly preferred for new projects because it guarantees each resource is torn down before the resource it depends on. [official]

---

### Pattern 127: Playwright `context.setStorageState()` inline user-switching — zero-overhead identity swap within a single test (TypeScript, Playwright 1.59+)

Rather than creating a new `BrowserContext` to test multi-role flows, `context.setStorageState()` atomically replaces auth cookies and localStorage in the current context. This avoids the latency of spawning a fresh browser context mid-test.

```typescript
// tests/fixtures/multi-role.fixture.ts
import { test as base } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'node:path';

interface MultiRoleFixtures {
  loginAs: (role: 'admin' | 'viewer' | 'editor') => Promise<void>;
}

export const test = base.extend<MultiRoleFixtures>({
  async loginAs({ context }, use) {
    const storageFor = (role: string) =>
      path.resolve(`playwright/.auth/${role}.json`);

    await use(async (role) => {
      // Atomically swap auth state in the running context — no new context needed
      await context.setStorageState({ path: storageFor(role) });
    });
  },
});

// tests/permission-check.test.ts
import { expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { test } from './fixtures/multi-role.fixture.js';

test('admin sees delete button, viewer does not', async ({ page, loginAs }) => {
  await loginAs('viewer');
  await page.goto('/documents/123');
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' })).toBeHidden();

  // Swap to admin in the same context — no new browser, no new page
  await loginAs('admin');
  await page.reload(); // reload with new auth cookies active
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Delete' })).toBeVisible();
});

test('editor can edit, viewer gets read-only form', async ({ page, loginAs }) => {
  await loginAs('editor');
  await page.goto('/documents/456/edit');
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /title/i })).toBeEnabled();

  await loginAs('viewer');
  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /title/i })).toBeDisabled();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `setStorageState()` is faster than `browser.newContext()` but shares the same browser-process memory between roles. Any browser-side JavaScript state (window globals, in-memory caches, WebSocket connections) from the previous role persists until a full navigation or reload. Always call `page.reload()` or `page.goto()` after `setStorageState()` to ensure the application bootstraps cleanly under the new identity. [official]

---

### Pattern 128: Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` — surfacing leaked `setTimeout` / `setInterval` / open sockets after each test (TypeScript, Vitest 4.1+)

`detectAsyncLeaks: true` instruments `node:async_hooks` to detect any async resource (timers, open handles, active requests) that was created during a test and not cleaned up before the test ends. It prints source locations for leaked resources.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    detectAsyncLeaks: true, // Vitest 4.1+
  },
});
```

```typescript
// src/polling-service.ts
export class PollingService {
  private timer?: NodeJS.Timeout;

  start(intervalMs: number, callback: () => void): void {
    this.timer = setInterval(callback, intervalMs);
  }

  stop(): void {
    if (this.timer) {
      clearInterval(this.timer);
      this.timer = undefined;
    }
  }
}

// tests/polling-service.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import { PollingService } from '../src/polling-service.js';

describe('PollingService', () => {
  let svc: PollingService;

  afterEach(() => {
    // Without this, detectAsyncLeaks reports the setInterval as a leak
    svc.stop();
  });

  it('invokes callback on interval', async () => {
    svc = new PollingService();
    const calls: number[] = [];
    svc.start(50, () => calls.push(Date.now()));

    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 180));
    expect(calls.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
  });

  it('stop() prevents further invocations', async () => {
    svc = new PollingService();
    const calls: number[] = [];
    svc.start(50, () => calls.push(1));
    svc.stop();

    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 150));
    expect(calls).toHaveLength(0);
    // afterEach calls stop() again — double-stop is safe because timer is already undefined
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `detectAsyncLeaks` adds per-test instrumentation overhead via `async_hooks` — expect a 5–15% slowdown in large suites. It also reports false positives from some third-party libraries that maintain deliberate background handles (e.g., database connection pools using `keepAlive`). Scope `detectAsyncLeaks` only to unit test projects where all resources are expected to be ephemeral; disable it in integration test projects that use connection pools. [official]

---

### Pattern 129: Jest `resetModules` + per-test `require()` — isolating singleton initializers that read `process.env` at module load time (TypeScript, Jest 27+)

Some modules execute side effects at import time (reading `process.env`, establishing a default configuration, registering global interceptors). `jest.resetModules()` combined with inline `require()` forces the module to re-evaluate for each test, picking up per-test environment values.

```typescript
// src/config.ts — reads env at module load time
export const config = {
  apiUrl: process.env.API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
  timeout: parseInt(process.env.TIMEOUT_MS ?? '5000', 10),
  debug: process.env.DEBUG === 'true',
} as const;

// tests/config.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';

describe('config', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    jest.resetModules(); // clear module registry before each test
  });

  it('uses API_URL from environment', () => {
    process.env.API_URL = 'https://api.prod.example.com';
    // Inline require() — evaluated AFTER resetModules + env mutation
    const { config } = require('../src/config.js') as typeof import('../src/config.js');
    expect(config.apiUrl).toBe('https://api.prod.example.com');
  });

  it('falls back to localhost when API_URL is unset', () => {
    delete process.env.API_URL;
    const { config } = require('../src/config.js') as typeof import('../src/config.js');
    expect(config.apiUrl).toBe('http://localhost:3000');
  });

  it('parses TIMEOUT_MS as integer', () => {
    process.env.API_URL = 'https://staging.example.com';
    process.env.TIMEOUT_MS = '10000';
    const { config } = require('../src/config.js') as typeof import('../src/config.js');
    expect(config.timeout).toBe(10000);
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Restore env to avoid leaking into tests in other files
    delete process.env.API_URL;
    delete process.env.TIMEOUT_MS;
    delete process.env.DEBUG;
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** This pattern requires `require()` — it does not work with static top-level `import` statements (ESM). For ESM modules, use `jest.unstable_mockModule()` + dynamic `await import()` instead, or use Vitest's `vi.stubEnv()` which handles the env mutation without requiring module re-evaluation. The `resetModules` pattern is reliable in CommonJS projects; avoid mixing static imports and `require()` in the same test file as TypeScript's module resolution may resolve them differently. [official]

---

### Pattern 130: Playwright `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial', retries: 0 })` — explicit ordering for multi-step integration flows with fail-fast (TypeScript, Playwright 1.10+)

For integration tests that represent a real sequential workflow (create → read → update → delete), serial mode combined with `retries: 0` ensures the entire scenario halts on first failure rather than running subsequent steps against corrupted state.

```typescript
// tests/order-lifecycle.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Runs sequentially; if step 1 fails, steps 2-4 are skipped automatically
test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial', retries: 0 });

let orderId: string;

test.describe('Order lifecycle — serial integration flow', () => {
  test('Step 1: create order', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/orders/new');
    await page.getByLabel('Product').selectOption('widget-pro');
    await page.getByLabel('Quantity').fill('3');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();

    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order #/i })).toBeVisible();
    orderId = (await page.getByTestId('order-id').innerText()).trim();
    expect(orderId).toMatch(/^ORD-\d+$/);
  });

  test('Step 2: view order details', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto(`/orders/${orderId}`);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-status')).toHaveText('Pending');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-quantity')).toHaveText('3');
  });

  test('Step 3: fulfil order via API then verify in UI', async ({ page, request }) => {
    await request.post(`/api/orders/${orderId}/fulfil`);
    await page.goto(`/orders/${orderId}`);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('order-status')).toHaveText('Fulfilled');
  });

  test('Step 4: cancel is disabled after fulfilment', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto(`/orders/${orderId}`);
    await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' })).toBeDisabled();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Serial mode trades test isolation for realistic scenario coverage. A failure in step 1 prevents all subsequent steps from running — the desired behaviour, but it can mask bugs in steps 2-4 that only surface when step 1 state is absent. Do NOT use serial mode for unit or component tests. Keep serial describe blocks small (4-8 steps). Always pair with unique per-run data identifiers (e.g., `orderId`) to avoid cross-run state collisions in shared staging environments. [official]

---

### Pattern 131: Vitest `vi.stubEnv` + `vi.unstubAllEnvs` — declarative environment variable isolation without raw `process.env` mutation (TypeScript, Vitest 0.26+)

`vi.stubEnv()` and `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` provide a declarative, restorable API for mutating `process.env` in tests. Unlike direct `process.env.FOO = 'bar'` assignment, `unstubAllEnvs()` restores original values even if the original value was `undefined`.

```typescript
// src/feature-flags.ts
export function isFeatureEnabled(flag: string): boolean {
  return process.env[`FEATURE_${flag.toUpperCase()}`] === 'true';
}

// tests/feature-flags.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';
import { isFeatureEnabled } from '../src/feature-flags.js';

describe('isFeatureEnabled', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.unstubAllEnvs(); // restore all env mutations — no manual cleanup needed
  });

  it('returns true when the env flag is "true"', () => {
    vi.stubEnv('FEATURE_DARK_MODE', 'true');
    expect(isFeatureEnabled('dark_mode')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('returns false when the env flag is "false"', () => {
    vi.stubEnv('FEATURE_DARK_MODE', 'false');
    expect(isFeatureEnabled('dark_mode')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('returns false when the env flag is absent', () => {
    // Ensure the key is definitely not set
    vi.stubEnv('FEATURE_DARK_MODE', undefined as unknown as string);
    expect(isFeatureEnabled('dark_mode')).toBe(false);
  });

  it('stubs multiple flags independently', () => {
    vi.stubEnv('FEATURE_NEW_CHECKOUT', 'true');
    vi.stubEnv('FEATURE_LEGACY_CART', 'false');
    expect(isFeatureEnabled('new_checkout')).toBe(true);
    expect(isFeatureEnabled('legacy_cart')).toBe(false);
    // Both stubs cleared by afterEach vi.unstubAllEnvs()
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `vi.stubEnv` only affects `process.env` — it does NOT force re-evaluation of modules that captured `process.env.FOO` at import time into a `const`. For those modules, combine `vi.stubEnv` with `vi.resetModules()` and re-import the module inside the test. In Vitest, `vi.stubEnv` is preferred over the Jest pattern of `process.env.FOO = ...; afterEach(() => delete process.env.FOO)` because the stub/unstub pair correctly handles keys that were originally missing (restoring `undefined` rather than leaving the key present with an empty string). [official]

---

### Pattern 132: Node.js `worker_threads` `workerData` namespace-scoping — isolating parallel worker state in tests that spawn real workers (TypeScript, Node.js 12+)

When testing code that spawns `worker_threads` Workers, each test must pass distinct `workerData` namespaces to prevent workers from sharing in-memory state through a global `BroadcastChannel` or a module-level singleton.

```typescript
// src/image-processor.worker.ts
import { workerData, parentPort } from 'node:worker_threads';

interface WorkerInput {
  workerId: string; // namespace key for isolation
  imagePath: string;
}

const { workerId, imagePath } = workerData as WorkerInput;
const result = { workerId, processed: imagePath.replace(/\.(jpg|png)$/, '.webp') };
parentPort?.postMessage(result);

// tests/image-processor.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { Worker } from 'node:worker_threads';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const WORKER_PATH = resolve(
  fileURLToPath(new URL('.', import.meta.url)),
  '../src/image-processor.worker.js'
);

function runWorker(
  workerId: string,
  imagePath: string
): Promise<{ workerId: string; processed: string }> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const worker = new Worker(WORKER_PATH, { workerData: { workerId, imagePath } });
    worker.once('message', resolve);
    worker.once('error', reject);
    worker.once('exit', (code) => {
      if (code !== 0) reject(new Error(`Worker exited with code ${code}`));
    });
  });
}

describe('image-processor worker', () => {
  it('converts .jpg to .webp', async () => {
    const result = await runWorker('test-1', '/images/photo.jpg');
    expect(result.workerId).toBe('test-1');
    expect(result.processed).toBe('/images/photo.webp');
  });

  it('converts .png to .webp', async () => {
    const result = await runWorker('test-2', '/images/icon.png');
    expect(result.workerId).toBe('test-2');
    expect(result.processed).toBe('/images/icon.webp');
  });

  it('two workers run concurrently without cross-contamination', async () => {
    const [r1, r2] = await Promise.all([
      runWorker('concurrent-1', '/a/image.jpg'),
      runWorker('concurrent-2', '/b/graphic.png'),
    ]);
    expect(r1.workerId).toBe('concurrent-1');
    expect(r2.workerId).toBe('concurrent-2');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Each `new Worker()` spawns a real OS thread with a cold-start cost. Keep worker-spawning tests in their own `describe` block and consider a `beforeAll` factory pattern that starts a pool of pre-warmed workers reused across tests in the suite. For tests that don't require real parallelism (e.g., testing `workerData` parsing logic), mock `worker_threads` entirely instead of spawning workers. [community]

---

### Pattern 133: MSW v2 `server.use()` per-test handler + `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` — layered network isolation for API-dependent tests (TypeScript, MSW 2.x)

MSW's `use()` call pushes a new handler to the top of the handler stack. `resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` pops all per-test handlers, restoring the base set. This provides a clean three-tier override model: global defaults → suite overrides → test overrides.

```typescript
// test-utils/msw-server.ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';

export const server = setupServer(
  http.get('https://api.example.com/users/:id', ({ params }) => {
    return HttpResponse.json({ id: params.id, name: 'Default User', role: 'viewer' });
  }),
  http.post('https://api.example.com/users', () => {
    return HttpResponse.json({ id: 'new-user-1' }, { status: 201 });
  })
);

// tests/user-profile.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, beforeAll, afterEach, afterAll } from 'vitest';
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw';
import { server } from '../test-utils/msw-server.js';
import { fetchUserProfile } from '../src/user-service.js';

beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }));
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers()); // clears per-test overrides only
afterAll(() => server.close());

describe('fetchUserProfile', () => {
  it('returns user data for a valid ID (uses base handler)', async () => {
    const profile = await fetchUserProfile('42');
    expect(profile.name).toBe('Default User');
    expect(profile.role).toBe('viewer');
  });

  it('handles admin users with per-test override', async () => {
    server.use(
      http.get('https://api.example.com/users/:id', () => {
        return HttpResponse.json({ id: '99', name: 'Admin Alice', role: 'admin' });
      })
    );
    const profile = await fetchUserProfile('99');
    expect(profile.role).toBe('admin');
    // afterEach resetHandlers() removes this override — next test sees base handler
  });

  it('handles 404 responses gracefully', async () => {
    server.use(
      http.get('https://api.example.com/users/:id', () => {
        return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 404 });
      })
    );
    await expect(fetchUserProfile('missing')).rejects.toThrow(/not found/i);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `server.use()` with `{ once: true }` does NOT remove the handler entry from the stack after it fires — it only prevents it from matching more than once. The handler entry remains until `resetHandlers()` is called. Relying on `once: true` as a substitute for `afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers())` causes subtle bugs when a test runs the handler-triggering path multiple times (retries, re-renders). Always use `resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` regardless of whether handlers were registered with `once: true`. [community]

---

### Pattern 134: Vitest `aroundEach` + Prisma interactive transactions — guaranteed rollback isolation for database integration tests (TypeScript, Vitest 4.1+)

`aroundEach` wraps each test in a single function that owns both setup and teardown, making it impossible to leak a test's database changes to the next test even if the test throws.

```typescript
// test-utils/db-rollback.fixture.ts
import { test as baseTest } from 'vitest';
import { PrismaClient, type Prisma } from '@prisma/client';

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

interface DbFixtures {
  tx: Prisma.TransactionClient;
}

export const test = baseTest.extend<DbFixtures>({
  async tx({ onCleanup }, use) {
    let resolveTest!: () => void;

    const txPromise = prisma.$transaction(
      async (client) => {
        await use(client as Prisma.TransactionClient);
        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => { resolveTest = resolve; });
        throw new Error('TEST_ROLLBACK'); // always rollback — never commit
      },
      { maxWait: 10000, timeout: 30000 }
    );

    onCleanup(async () => {
      resolveTest?.();
      try {
        await txPromise;
      } catch (e) {
        if ((e as Error).message !== 'TEST_ROLLBACK') throw e;
        // Expected rollback error — swallow
      }
    });
  },
});

// tests/user-repository.test.ts
import { expect } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '../test-utils/db-rollback.fixture.js';

test('creates a user and reads it back within the transaction', async ({ tx }) => {
  const created = await tx.user.create({
    data: { email: 'alice@example.com', name: 'Alice' },
  });
  expect(created.id).toBeDefined();

  const found = await tx.user.findUnique({ where: { id: created.id } });
  expect(found?.email).toBe('alice@example.com');
  // Transaction rolled back after test — alice@example.com never committed
});

test('second test starts with empty users table', async ({ tx }) => {
  const count = await tx.user.count();
  expect(count).toBe(0); // previous test's changes were rolled back
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Prisma interactive transactions hold a database connection for the duration of the test. On a connection pool of size N, running more than N parallel tests with this fixture will deadlock as all connections are held open waiting for tests to complete. Set `maxWorkers` to a value <= connection pool size, or use per-worker schemas as an alternative when tests are highly parallel. [community]

---

### Pattern 135: Jest `jest.replaceProperty()` + `jest.Replaced<T>` — type-safe non-configurable property isolation (TypeScript, Jest 29.4+)

Non-configurable object properties (e.g., `process.platform`, `navigator.userAgent`, `process.version`) cannot be replaced by `jest.spyOn()`. `jest.replaceProperty()` bypasses this restriction and returns a typed `jest.Replaced<T>` handle for restoration.

```typescript
// src/platform-guard.ts
export function requireLinux(): void {
  if (process.platform !== 'linux') {
    throw new Error(`This feature requires Linux. Got: ${process.platform}`);
  }
}

export function getNodeMajorVersion(): number {
  return parseInt(process.version.slice(1).split('.')[0], 10);
}

// tests/platform-guard.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { requireLinux, getNodeMajorVersion } from '../src/platform-guard.js';

describe('requireLinux', () => {
  let platformRestore: jest.Replaced<typeof process.platform>;

  afterEach(() => {
    platformRestore?.restore(); // always restore — non-configurable property persists if not restored
  });

  it('passes on linux', () => {
    platformRestore = jest.replaceProperty(process, 'platform', 'linux' as NodeJS.Platform);
    expect(() => requireLinux()).not.toThrow();
  });

  it('throws on win32', () => {
    platformRestore = jest.replaceProperty(process, 'platform', 'win32' as NodeJS.Platform);
    expect(() => requireLinux()).toThrow(/requires Linux/);
  });
});

describe('getNodeMajorVersion', () => {
  let versionRestore: jest.Replaced<typeof process.version>;

  afterEach(() => versionRestore?.restore());

  it('parses major version from process.version', () => {
    versionRestore = jest.replaceProperty(process, 'version', 'v20.11.0');
    expect(getNodeMajorVersion()).toBe(20);
  });

  it('handles single-digit major', () => {
    versionRestore = jest.replaceProperty(process, 'version', 'v8.17.0');
    expect(getNodeMajorVersion()).toBe(8);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `jest.replaceProperty()` stores the original value and restores it on `.restore()`. Unlike `jest.spyOn()`, it does not track calls or allow `.mockImplementation()` — it only sets a new value. If the test throws before `restore()` is called, the property remains mutated for subsequent tests in the same worker unless `afterEach` guarantees restoration. Always store the return value and call `.restore()` in `afterEach`, never inline in the test body. [official]

---

### Pattern 136: Vitest `vi.stubGlobal` + `vi.unstubAllGlobals` — safe global API replacement with guaranteed teardown (TypeScript, Vitest 0.26+)

`vi.stubGlobal(key, value)` replaces a global (e.g., `fetch`, `crypto`, `localStorage`) with a controlled substitute, while `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach` restores all stubs in a single call regardless of how many were registered in the test.

```typescript
// src/analytics-client.ts
export async function trackEvent(event: string, data: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void> {
  await fetch('/api/analytics', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ event, data, timestamp: Date.now() }),
  });
}

// tests/analytics-client.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach, vi } from 'vitest';
import { trackEvent } from '../src/analytics-client.js';

describe('trackEvent', () => {
  afterEach(() => {
    vi.unstubAllGlobals(); // restores global fetch to original
  });

  it('POSTs the event payload to /api/analytics', async () => {
    const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(
      new Response(null, { status: 204 })
    );
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);

    await trackEvent('page_view', { path: '/home' });

    expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    const [url, init] = fetchMock.mock.calls[0] as [string, RequestInit];
    expect(url).toBe('/api/analytics');
    expect(JSON.parse(init.body as string)).toMatchObject({
      event: 'page_view',
      data: { path: '/home' },
    });
  });

  it('does not throw when analytics endpoint returns 500', async () => {
    vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(
      new Response(null, { status: 500 })
    ));
    // trackEvent ignores non-2xx — fire-and-forget analytics pattern
    await expect(trackEvent('error_event', {})).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `vi.stubGlobal` replaces the property on `globalThis` directly and does not wrap it (unlike `vi.spyOn`), so the stub is not callable on the original. If you need to intercept calls while preserving the original fallback (e.g., spy on `fetch` but let some requests through), use a `vi.fn().mockImplementation(originalFetch)` wrapper and pass it to `stubGlobal`. `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` only restores keys that were explicitly stubbed via `vi.stubGlobal` — manual `globalThis.fetch = mockFn` assignments are not tracked and must be cleaned up manually. [official]

---

## Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 27

166. **Vitest `test.extend` builder pattern `onCleanup` must be called synchronously inside the fixture's own async function — calling it from an asynchronous helper after `use()` returns silently drops the registration.** [community]
    The builder pattern's `onCleanup` parameter is only valid during the synchronous execution of the fixture's setup phase (before `await use(...)`). Registering `onCleanup` in a helper that executes asynchronously after `use()` returns silently drops the registration — no error is thrown, no cleanup runs. Always call `onCleanup` before `await use(...)` and inline, not inside a separately-awaited helper function.

167. **Jest `doNotFake` property names are case-sensitive and must match the exact key on `globalThis` — a typo like `'date'` instead of `'Date'` is silently ignored, leaving `Date` faked.** [community]
    The `doNotFake` array in `jest.useFakeTimers({ doNotFake: ['Date'] })` is case-sensitive. A typo like `'date'` is silently ignored — `Date` gets faked as normal with no warning. Always verify the global property name by checking `Object.keys(globalThis)` or the Node.js / browser documentation, not by guessing casing.

168. **Playwright worker-scoped fixtures are NOT torn down when a worker is killed by `--bail` — only test-scoped fixture teardown code runs on bail.** [community]
    When `--bail 1` causes Playwright to terminate a worker after the first failure, the worker-scoped fixture teardown code (after `await use()`) is not reached. Database users provisioned in worker-scoped fixtures survive the test run and must be cleaned by a separate `globalTeardown` script. Use test-scoped fixtures for resources that must always be cleaned up, or accept that worker-scoped fixture teardown is best-effort under bail conditions.

169. **Vitest `sequence.hooks: 'stack'` became the default in Vitest 4.0 — upgrading from Vitest 3.x silently reverses teardown order in suites that relied on FIFO `afterAll` behaviour.** [community]
    Code that relied on `afterAll` hooks running in the same order they were registered (FIFO / `'list'`) now runs in reverse order (LIFO / `'stack'`) after upgrading to Vitest 4.0+. The most common symptom is a resource being closed before another resource that depends on it has finished. Audit `describe` blocks with multiple `afterAll` hooks when upgrading; add `sequence: { hooks: 'list' }` to restore previous behaviour if needed.

170. **Jest `restoreMocks: true` silently has no effect on `jest.mock('./module')` factory mocks — these remain active until `jest.unmock()` or `jest.resetModules()` is called explicitly.** [community]
    `restoreMocks` only restores `jest.spyOn` wrappers to their original implementations. Factory mocks registered with `jest.mock()` bypass the `restoreMocks` lifecycle entirely. Teams that adopt `restoreMocks: true` expecting all mocks to be cleared between tests and then use `jest.mock()` at the top of test files will find the factory mock persists for the entire file even with `restoreMocks: true` active. Document which clearing mechanism applies to each mock type in your project's testing guidelines.

171. **Playwright `context.setStorageState()` does not clear Service Worker registrations — a cached SW from a prior role's auth session can intercept requests for the new role after an in-test user switch.** [community]
    `setStorageState()` replaces cookies and localStorage/sessionStorage. Service Worker registrations in the origin's SW scope are NOT cleared. If the application uses a SW that caches auth-scoped resources, the SW can serve stale responses from the previous role until the SW's own cache is invalidated. Unregister SWs via `page.evaluate(() => navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations().then(r => r.forEach(w => w.unregister())))` before calling `setStorageState()` when SWs are involved.

172. **Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` reports false positives for `node-postgres` (`pg`) connection pools — the pool's keep-alive handle is a legitimate background async resource, not a test leak.** [community]
    Database connection pools maintain background `setInterval` or socket keep-alive handles. These appear as leaked async resources when `detectAsyncLeaks: true` is enabled globally. The correct fix is NOT to close the pool after every test (that defeats pooling) but to scope `detectAsyncLeaks: true` only to unit test projects that cannot have legitimate background handles, and keep it disabled in integration test projects.

173. **MSW `{ once: true }` handler does not auto-remove its stack entry after matching — it only blocks re-matching, and stale entries accumulate if `resetHandlers()` is not called.** [community]
    Each call to `server.use(handler, { once: true })` appends a disabled-after-first-match entry to the handler stack. After many tests, the stack can contain dozens of stale entries. This does not cause incorrect responses but increases per-request handler-scan cost and can cause confusing trace output. Always call `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` to drain the stack, regardless of `{ once: true }` usage.

174. **Jest `resetModules` combined with `ts-jest` does not invalidate the TypeScript compilation cache — stale compiled output is used even after source-level changes in watch mode.** [community]
    `resetModules` clears Jest's module registry (require cache), forcing re-evaluation of JavaScript. However, `ts-jest` compiles TypeScript once per worker session and caches the compiled output. If a test relies on `resetModules` to pick up a TypeScript source change made during the test run (e.g., `fs.writeFileSync` modifying a source file), the cached compiled output will be used. This scenario is rare in CI but occurs in watch mode tests that write source files — use in-memory stubs instead of writing real source files.

175. **Playwright `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` applies only to the containing describe block — nested describe blocks default back to parallel unless they also configure serial mode explicitly.** [community]
    `serial` mode is not inherited by nested `describe` blocks. A serial outer describe with a default-parallel inner describe causes the inner tests to run concurrently, potentially overlapping with the outer serial flow's state. Always explicitly configure every nested `describe` that must participate in the serial execution order, including deeply nested blocks.

---

## Quick Reference — Cycle 27

| Problem | Symptom | Solution | Framework |
|---------|---------|----------|-----------|
| `onCleanup` called from async helper after `use()` | Teardown silently dropped; resources leaked | Call `onCleanup` synchronously before `await use(...)` in the fixture function | Vitest 4.1+ |
| `doNotFake` typo in `useFakeTimers` | Target global still faked; unexpected behaviour | Use exact `globalThis` key name (case-sensitive); verify against Node.js docs | Jest 27+ |
| Worker-scoped fixture not torn down on `--bail` | DB users / resources survive test run | Use test-scoped fixtures for must-clean resources; add `globalTeardown` safety-net | Playwright |
| Vitest 4.0 upgrade reverses `afterAll` order | Resource closed before dependent finishes | Audit multi-`afterAll` suites; add `sequence: { hooks: 'list' }` if FIFO required | Vitest 4.0+ |
| `restoreMocks: true` doesn't clear `jest.mock()` factory mocks | Factory mock persists across all tests in file | Use `jest.unmock()` or `jest.resetModules()` for factory mocks; `restoreMocks` = spyOn only | Jest 27+ |
| SW caches auth tokens after `setStorageState()` user switch | New role gets cached responses for prior role | Unregister SWs via `page.evaluate()` before `setStorageState()` | Playwright |
| `detectAsyncLeaks` false-positives from DB connection pool | Pool keep-alive handle flagged as test leak | Scope `detectAsyncLeaks: true` to unit test projects only | Vitest 4.1+ |
| MSW `{ once: true }` stale stack entries accumulate | Handler-scan overhead; confusing trace output | Always call `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` regardless of `once` | MSW 2.x |
| `ts-jest` compile cache stale after `resetModules` | Stale compiled module returned in watch mode | Use in-memory stubs; avoid writing source files during test runs | Jest + ts-jest |
| `serial` mode not inherited by nested `describe` | Inner tests run concurrently with outer serial state | Explicitly configure each nested `describe` that must be serial | Playwright |
| Prisma transaction fixture deadlocks under high parallelism | Tests hang waiting for DB connection | Cap `maxWorkers` <= pool size; or use per-worker schemas | Vitest + Prisma |
| `parallelIndex` vs `workerIndex` confusion on retry | DB user slot collision on re-run | Use `parallelIndex` (stable slot) not `workerIndex` (reassigned after crash) | Playwright 1.40+ |
| `vi.stubEnv` doesn't force module re-evaluation | Module reads old captured `process.env` value | Combine `vi.stubEnv` with `vi.resetModules()` + dynamic `await import()` | Vitest |
| `jest.replaceProperty` not restored on test throw | Non-configurable property mutated in next tests | Store return value; call `.restore()` in `afterEach`, not inline in test body | Jest 29.4+ |
| `vi.unstubAllGlobals` does not restore manual `globalThis` assignments | Manually set global persists between tests | Only use `vi.stubGlobal()` (not manual `globalThis.x = ...`) for stubs needing auto-restore | Vitest |

### Pattern 137: Jest 30 case-sensitive `jest.mock()` path enforcement — strict module isolation in cross-platform repos  [official]

Jest 30 enforces exact case-sensitive paths for `jest.mock()` calls. On case-insensitive filesystems (macOS, Windows), Jest 29 silently matched `./path/to/FILENAME.js` to a file named `filename.js`. Jest 30 rejects the mismatch, preventing a class of bugs where the wrong module was intercepted (or not intercepted) depending on OS casing conventions.

```typescript
// src/emailService.ts
export async function sendWelcomeEmail(to: string): Promise<void> {
  const { mailerTransport } = await import('./MailerTransport');
  await mailerTransport.send({ to, subject: 'Welcome' });
}

// tests/emailService.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';

// Jest 30: path must match EXACTLY — 'MailerTransport', not 'mailertransport'
jest.mock('./MailerTransport', () => ({
  mailerTransport: {
    send: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined),
  },
}));

import { sendWelcomeEmail } from '../src/emailService';
import { mailerTransport } from '../src/MailerTransport';

const mockSend = jest.mocked(mailerTransport).send;

describe('sendWelcomeEmail', () => {
  beforeEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks());

  it('delegates to mailerTransport.send with correct address', async () => {
    await sendWelcomeEmail('alice@example.com');
    expect(mockSend).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(mockSend).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ to: 'alice@example.com' })
    );
  });

  it('does not throw when transport succeeds', async () => {
    await expect(sendWelcomeEmail('bob@example.com')).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: migrating a Jest 29 suite to Jest 30 — audit all `jest.mock()` paths for casing before upgrading to avoid runtime "cannot find module" errors that only appear on Linux CI. Do NOT rely on case-insensitive matching as a workaround — it was a latent bug, not a feature. Alternative: `moduleNameMapper` in config with a regex key provides a canonical redirect that is always case-correct. [official]

### Pattern 138: `jest.waitForUnhandledRejections` — async teardown isolation for unhandled promise rejections  [official]

Jest 30 adds `waitForUnhandledRejections` (default `true`) which waits an extra event-loop turn after each test before checking for unhandled rejections. This prevents false-positive failures where a rejection from test A was attributed to test B. Set to `false` only when async teardown itself must complete synchronously.

```typescript
// src/backgroundQueue.ts
export class BackgroundQueue {
  private running = false;

  async processNext(): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.running) return;
    // Simulates a rejection that fires after test body returns
    await Promise.reject(new Error('Queue processing failure'));
  }

  start(): void { this.running = true; }
  stop(): void { this.running = false; }
}

// tests/backgroundQueue.test.ts
// jest.config.ts: waitForUnhandledRejections: true (default in Jest 30)
import { describe, it, expect, afterEach } from '@jest/globals';
import { BackgroundQueue } from '../src/backgroundQueue';

describe('BackgroundQueue', () => {
  let queue: BackgroundQueue;

  beforeEach(() => {
    queue = new BackgroundQueue();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Ensure async errors from this test are attributed here, not to next test
    queue.stop();
  });

  it('does not process when not started', async () => {
    // queue.processNext() returns immediately when !running — no rejection
    await expect(queue.processNext()).resolves.toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('rejects when started and processNext is called', async () => {
    queue.start();
    await expect(queue.processNext()).rejects.toThrow('Queue processing failure');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: tests fire async side-effects that reject after the test body completes (fire-and-forget patterns, event-driven callbacks). Do NOT set `waitForUnhandledRejections: false` unless your entire test suite has no async side-effects — the default is safer. Named alternative: wrap async side-effects in try/catch to prevent unhandled rejections entirely. [official]

### Pattern 139: Vitest `test.signal` (AbortSignal) — in-flight async resource cancellation on timeout/bail  [official]

Vitest 3.2+ provides `test.signal` (an `AbortSignal`) that is aborted when the test times out, when `--bail` triggers, or when the user presses Ctrl+C. Pass it to `fetch`, `ReadableStream`, or any Web API that accepts `AbortSignal` to cancel in-flight work without manual teardown code.

```typescript
// src/dataFetcher.ts
export async function fetchPagedData(
  url: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal
): Promise<string[]> {
  const results: string[] = [];
  let cursor: string | null = null;

  do {
    const fullUrl = cursor ? `${url}?cursor=${cursor}` : url;
    const response = await fetch(fullUrl, { signal });
    const json = await response.json() as { items: string[]; next: string | null };
    results.push(...json.items);
    cursor = json.next;
  } while (cursor);

  return results;
}

// tests/dataFetcher.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';
import { fetchPagedData } from '../src/dataFetcher';

describe('fetchPagedData', () => {
  it('passes test.signal to fetch so in-flight requests abort on test timeout', async (ctx) => {
    const fetchSpy = vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockResolvedValue(
      new Response(JSON.stringify({ items: ['a', 'b'], next: null }), {
        status: 200,
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      })
    );

    const result = await fetchPagedData('https://api.example.com/items', ctx.signal);

    expect(result).toEqual(['a', 'b']);
    expect(fetchSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      'https://api.example.com/items',
      expect.objectContaining({ signal: ctx.signal })
    );
  });

  it('stops pagination when signal is aborted mid-page', async () => {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    const fetchSpy = vi.spyOn(globalThis, 'fetch').mockImplementation(async (url) => {
      if (String(url).includes('cursor=page2')) {
        controller.abort();
        throw new DOMException('Aborted', 'AbortError');
      }
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({ items: ['x'], next: 'page2' }));
    });

    await expect(
      fetchPagedData('https://api.example.com/items', controller.signal)
    ).rejects.toThrow('Aborted');
    expect(fetchSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: tests exercise paginated APIs, streaming endpoints, or long-polling code that must not leave hanging connections when the test is cancelled. Do NOT use when the code under test does not accept `AbortSignal` — there is no benefit. Alternative: wrap long async work in `Promise.race([originalPromise, abortPromise])` for older APIs that predate AbortController. [official]

---

### Pattern 140: Playwright `page.clock.install()` before `page.goto()` — deterministic time travel without JSDOM  [official]

Playwright v1.45+ `page.clock.install({ time })` sets the browser's `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `performance.now()` to a fixed starting point before the page loads, ensuring all client-side timers start from a known epoch. Unlike JSDOM-based fake timers, this affects the real Chromium/WebKit/Firefox JS engine.

```typescript
// tests/session-timeout.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('session timeout banner', () => {
  // Fix time at a known moment so tests are deterministic across machines/TZs
  const SESSION_START_MS = new Date('2026-01-15T09:00:00.000Z').getTime();

  test('shows warning banner 5 minutes before session expires', async ({ page }) => {
    // Install clock BEFORE goto so first JS evaluation uses controlled time
    await page.clock.install({ time: SESSION_START_MS });

    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Session timeout is 30 min; warning shows at 25 min elapsed
    await page.clock.fastForward('25:00');

    const banner = page.locator('[data-testid="session-warning"]');
    await expect(banner).toBeVisible();
    await expect(banner).toContainText('Your session expires in 5 minutes');
  });

  test('redirects to /login exactly at session expiry', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.clock.install({ time: SESSION_START_MS });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Advance full 30 minutes
    await page.clock.fastForward('30:00');

    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  });

  test('resets timeout on user activity', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.clock.install({ time: SESSION_START_MS });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    await page.clock.fastForward('20:00');
    // Simulate user activity that resets the timer
    await page.locator('body').click();
    // Advance another 25 min — timer was reset at 20 min mark
    await page.clock.fastForward('25:00');

    const banner = page.locator('[data-testid="session-warning"]');
    await expect(banner).not.toBeVisible();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: testing session timeouts, token refresh windows, auto-save intervals, or any UI behavior that depends on `Date.now()` or `setTimeout`. Do NOT use on pages where real-time WebSocket or SSE data is expected — frozen time prevents live data from arriving. Alternative: Jest/Vitest `useFakeTimers()` works for unit tests but cannot control a real browser's JS engine. [official]

### Pattern 141: Vitest `aroundEach` + Knex transaction rollback — single-closure DB isolation without beforeEach/afterEach pairing  [official]

Vitest 4.1+ `aroundEach` provides a single closure enclosing both setup and teardown, guaranteed to run teardown even if the test throws. This is safer than `beforeEach`/`afterEach` pairs because the connection handle is scoped to the closure and cannot leak.

```typescript
// tests/helpers/knexFixture.ts
import { AsyncLocalStorage } from 'node:async_hooks';
import knex, { type Knex } from 'knex';

const db = knex({ client: 'pg', connection: process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL });
export const currentTrx = new AsyncLocalStorage<Knex.Transaction>();

export async function withRolledBackTransaction(
  runTest: () => Promise<void>
): Promise<void> {
  const trx = await db.transaction();
  await currentTrx.run(trx, async () => {
    try {
      await runTest();
    } finally {
      // Rollback always — whether test passed, failed, or threw
      await trx.rollback();
    }
  });
}

// tests/userRepository.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, aroundEach } from 'vitest';
import { withRolledBackTransaction, currentTrx } from './helpers/knexFixture';
import { UserRepository } from '../src/userRepository';

describe('UserRepository', () => {
  aroundEach(withRolledBackTransaction);

  it('creates a user and finds it within the transaction', async () => {
    const trx = currentTrx.getStore()!;
    const repo = new UserRepository(trx);

    const user = await repo.create({ name: 'Charlie', email: 'charlie@example.com' });
    const found = await repo.findById(user.id);

    expect(found?.name).toBe('Charlie');
    // Rollback fires in aroundEach — next test sees empty DB
  });

  it('finds no users after rollback from previous test', async () => {
    const trx = currentTrx.getStore()!;
    const repo = new UserRepository(trx);

    const all = await repo.findAll();
    expect(all).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: Vitest 4.1+ is available and you want the strongest guarantee that teardown runs even on exception. Do NOT use when your ORM does not support nested transactions or when the production code opens its own transaction internally (the inner transaction cannot see the outer test transaction). Alternative: Prisma `$transaction` + `aroundEach` (Pattern 134); TypeORM `queryRunner.rollbackTransaction()` in `afterEach`. [official]

---

### Pattern 142: Jest 30 `moduleFileExtensions` `.mts`/`.cts` — native TypeScript ESM/CJS module isolation  [official]

Jest 30 adds `.mts` and `.cts` to the default `moduleFileExtensions` list, enabling ES Module (`.mts`) and CommonJS (`.cts`) TypeScript files to be resolved and mocked without manual `moduleFileExtensions` configuration. This closes an isolation gap where `jest.mock('./path.mts')` silently fell through to the real module in Jest 29.

```typescript
// src/featureFlags.mts  (ES module TypeScript)
export async function isFeatureEnabled(flag: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { remoteConfig } = await import('./remoteConfig.mts');
  return remoteConfig.get(flag) === 'true';
}

// src/remoteConfig.mts
export const remoteConfig = {
  get: (_key: string): string => {
    throw new Error('remoteConfig.get() must not be called in tests');
  },
};

// tests/featureFlags.test.mts
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';

// Jest 30: .mts extension resolved correctly in default moduleFileExtensions
jest.mock('../src/remoteConfig.mts', () => ({
  remoteConfig: {
    get: jest.fn(),
  },
}));

import { isFeatureEnabled } from '../src/featureFlags.mts';
import { remoteConfig } from '../src/remoteConfig.mts';

const mockGet = jest.mocked(remoteConfig.get);

describe('isFeatureEnabled', () => {
  beforeEach(() => jest.clearAllMocks());

  it('returns true when remote config returns "true"', async () => {
    mockGet.mockReturnValue('true');
    await expect(isFeatureEnabled('dark-mode')).resolves.toBe(true);
  });

  it('returns false when remote config returns any other value', async () => {
    mockGet.mockReturnValue('disabled');
    await expect(isFeatureEnabled('dark-mode')).resolves.toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: your codebase uses `.mts` or `.cts` files (TypeScript ESM/CJS explicit extensions). Do NOT add `.mts`/`.cts` to `moduleFileExtensions` manually in Jest 30+ — they are already included by default and duplicating them causes resolver warnings. Alternative: `jest.unstable_mockModule` for ESM mocks that require dynamic import after mock registration. [official]

---

### Pattern 143: Vitest `file`-scoped fixture — expensive per-file setup without shared module singletons  [official]

Vitest 3.2+ `scope: 'file'` fixtures initialize once per test file (not once per worker), providing the right granularity for expensive per-file resources (compiled schemas, seed data) without sharing state across files. Unlike `beforeAll`, file-scoped fixtures compose with other fixtures via the `test.extend` API.

```typescript
// tests/fixtures/compiledSchema.ts
import { test as base } from 'vitest';
import { buildSchema, type GraphQLSchema } from 'graphql';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';

type SchemaFixture = { schema: GraphQLSchema };

// Scope: 'file' — compiled once per test file, not once per test
export const test = base.extend<SchemaFixture>({
  schema: [
    async ({}, use) => {
      const sdl = readFileSync('./schema.graphql', 'utf8');
      const schema = buildSchema(sdl); // Expensive: ~100ms
      await use(schema);
      // Teardown: nothing to release for an in-memory compiled schema
    },
    { scope: 'file' },
  ],
});

// tests/graphql/queryResolution.test.ts
import { expect } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '../fixtures/compiledSchema';
import { graphql } from 'graphql';
import { createResolvers } from '../../src/resolvers';

test('resolves user query with correct fields', async ({ schema }) => {
  const resolvers = createResolvers({ userId: 'u1', name: 'Alice' });
  const result = await graphql({
    schema,
    source: '{ user { id name } }',
    rootValue: resolvers,
  });
  expect(result.errors).toBeUndefined();
  expect(result.data?.user).toMatchObject({ id: 'u1', name: 'Alice' });
});

test('returns null for unknown user', async ({ schema }) => {
  const resolvers = createResolvers(null);
  const result = await graphql({ schema, source: '{ user { id } }', rootValue: resolvers });
  expect(result.data?.user).toBeNull();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: setup is expensive (schema compilation, static asset parsing, certificate loading) and is safe to share within a single file (immutable after construction). Do NOT use for stateful resources like database connections — a test that mutates shared state affects all subsequent tests in the file. Alternative: `scope: 'worker'` for even coarser sharing (one instance per entire worker process), at the cost of cross-file state bleed. [official]

---

### Pattern 144: Playwright `page.clock.fastForward()` vs `page.clock.tick()` — precision time advancement isolation  [official]

Playwright's clock API has two advancement methods with distinct isolation semantics: `fastForward(ms)` skips to the future and fires all pending timers that would have expired, while `tick(ms)` advances time step by step, allowing intermediate timer callbacks to fire in order. Choosing the wrong method can leave timer callbacks in different states across tests.

```typescript
// tests/autoSave.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000; // 30 seconds

test.describe('auto-save indicator', () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    // Clock installed before page load so timers fire at predictable intervals
    await page.clock.install({ time: Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1, 12, 0, 0) });
    await page.goto('/editor');
  });

  test('fastForward fires all pending autosave timers at once', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('[data-testid="editor"]').fill('Draft content');

    // fastForward: all timers that expire within 90s fire immediately
    await page.clock.fastForward(3 * AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS);

    const indicator = page.locator('[data-testid="save-indicator"]');
    await expect(indicator).toHaveText('Saved 3 times');
  });

  test('tick fires timers in order, allowing intermediate state assertions', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('[data-testid="editor"]').fill('Draft content');

    // tick: advance 30 seconds, assert save happened, then advance again
    await page.clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS);
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="save-indicator"]')).toHaveText('Saved 1 time');

    await page.clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS);
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="save-indicator"]')).toHaveText('Saved 2 times');
  });

  test('does not autosave when content is unchanged', async ({ page }) => {
    // No content change — autosave should be a no-op
    await page.clock.fastForward(2 * AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS);
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="save-indicator"]')).toHaveText('No unsaved changes');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** `fastForward` is appropriate when only the final state matters (e.g., verifying a banner appears after N minutes). `tick` is required when intermediate states must be asserted or when the order of timer callbacks matters (e.g., debounce + flush sequence). Do NOT mix `fastForward` and `tick` in the same test — the semantics interact unexpectedly when multiple timers compete. Alternative: real `page.waitForTimeout()` (but slow and non-deterministic in CI). [official]

---

### Pattern 145: Jest `using` keyword for automatic spy cleanup — explicit resource management in TypeScript 5.2+  [official]

TypeScript 5.2 `using` keyword integrates with Jest's `jest.spyOn()` return value, which implements `Symbol.dispose`. The spy is automatically restored when the `using` block exits — no `afterEach` needed and no risk of forgetting restoration when the test throws mid-assertion.

```typescript
// src/auditLogger.ts
export const auditLogger = {
  log(action: string, userId: string): void {
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ action, userId, ts: Date.now() }));
  },
};

// tests/auditLogger.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { auditLogger } from '../src/auditLogger';
import { processUserAction } from '../src/processor';

describe('processUserAction', () => {
  it('logs the action with the correct userId', () => {
    // 'using' auto-restores spy when this test scope exits — no afterEach needed
    using logSpy = jest.spyOn(auditLogger, 'log').mockImplementation(() => {});

    processUserAction({ action: 'DELETE_RECORD', userId: 'u99' });

    expect(logSpy).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(logSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith('DELETE_RECORD', 'u99');
  });

  it('does not call auditLogger for read-only actions', () => {
    // Independent spy scope — prior test's spy was fully restored
    using logSpy = jest.spyOn(auditLogger, 'log').mockImplementation(() => {});

    processUserAction({ action: 'READ_RECORD', userId: 'u99' });

    expect(logSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('still logs even when processor throws', () => {
    using logSpy = jest.spyOn(auditLogger, 'log').mockImplementation(() => {});
    // Even if this assertion fails and throws, the spy is restored by 'using'
    expect(() => processUserAction({ action: 'INVALID', userId: 'u1' })).toThrow();
    expect(logSpy).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: TypeScript 5.2+ is available and `lib` or `target` includes `ES2022` or later. Do NOT use in CommonJS modules compiled to ES5 — `Symbol.dispose` is not polyfilled by default. Alternative: `afterEach(() => jest.restoreAllMocks())` is the equivalent for projects without TypeScript 5.2+. [official]

---

### Pattern 146: Playwright `browserContext.addInitScript()` — per-context state injection before page load for hermetic isolation  [official]

`browserContext.addInitScript(fn)` runs a script in every page created in the context, before any page scripts execute. This is the correct place to stub `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `window.crypto.getRandomValues`, or any browser global that must be controlled before application code reads it on load — doing this in `page.evaluate()` after `goto()` is too late.

```typescript
// tests/featureToggle.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('feature toggle rendering', () => {
  test('renders beta UI when localStorage flag is set before page load', async ({
    browser,
  }) => {
    // Each test gets its own context — hermetically isolated from other tests
    const context = await browser.newContext();

    await context.addInitScript(() => {
      // Runs BEFORE application scripts evaluate localStorage
      window.localStorage.setItem('feature:beta-ui', 'enabled');
    });

    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="beta-badge"]')).toBeVisible();
    await context.close(); // Teardown — context and its localStorage wiped
  });

  test('renders stable UI when flag is absent', async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext();
    // No addInitScript — localStorage is empty by default in new context
    const page = await context.newPage();

    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="beta-badge"]')).not.toBeVisible();
    await context.close();
  });

  test('crypto.getRandomValues returns deterministic bytes for reproducible seeds', async ({
    browser,
  }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext();

    await context.addInitScript(() => {
      window.crypto.getRandomValues = function <T extends ArrayBufferView | null>(arr: T): T {
        // Deterministic fill for reproducible test seeds
        if (arr instanceof Uint8Array) arr.fill(42);
        return arr;
      };
    });

    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/generate-token');
    const token = await page.locator('[data-testid="token"]').innerText();

    // Token generated from deterministic random bytes is always the same
    expect(token).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{32}$/);
    await context.close();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: the application reads `localStorage`, feature flags, or global APIs during module initialization (before DOMContentLoaded). Do NOT use for authentication state that changes during the test — prefer `page.route()` or `setStorageState()` for mid-test auth manipulation. Alternative: `page.addInitScript()` targets a single page rather than the whole context; use the context-level version when multiple pages within the context need the same pre-load state. [official]

---

### Pattern 147: Vitest workspace `isolate: false` per-project override — selective isolation bypass for pure-computation modules  [official]

Vitest 4.0+ allows setting `isolate: false` at the project level in `vitest.workspace.ts`, disabling VM sandbox isolation for a specific subset of tests while keeping isolation enabled everywhere else. This is the correct pattern for performance-sensitive pure-function test projects that have no global side-effects.

```typescript
// vitest.workspace.ts
import { defineWorkspace } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineWorkspace([
  {
    // Unit tests for pure math/algorithm modules — no side-effects, skip VM overhead
    test: {
      name: 'fast-unit',
      include: ['src/algorithms/**/*.test.ts', 'src/utils/**/*.test.ts'],
      pool: 'threads',
      isolate: false,   // No per-test module registry reset — 3-5x faster
      environment: 'node',
    },
  },
  {
    // Integration tests — full isolation required; modules have singletons
    test: {
      name: 'integration',
      include: ['tests/integration/**/*.test.ts'],
      pool: 'forks',
      isolate: true,    // Default: each test file gets a fresh module registry
      environment: 'node',
    },
  },
  {
    // Browser component tests — always isolated
    test: {
      name: 'components',
      include: ['src/**/*.spec.tsx'],
      browser: { enabled: true, name: 'chromium', provider: 'playwright' },
      isolate: true,
    },
  },
]);

// Example pure-computation test that benefits from isolate: false
// src/algorithms/fibonacci.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { fibonacci } from './fibonacci';

describe('fibonacci', () => {
  it.each([
    [0, 0], [1, 1], [2, 1], [10, 55], [20, 6765],
  ] as const)('fib(%i) = %i', (n, expected) => {
    expect(fibonacci(n)).toBe(expected);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: the module has no module-level mutable state, does not import any singleton, and tests are 100% pure (no DB, no network, no `process.env` mutation). Do NOT use if any test in the project uses `vi.mock()`, `vi.resetModules()`, or mutates module-level state — the lack of isolation will cause cross-test contamination that is very hard to debug. Alternative: `pool: 'threads'` without `isolate: false` gives 50-70% of the speedup by reusing worker threads while keeping module isolation. [official]

---

### Pattern 148: `node:test` `TestContext.mock.timers` with `setTime()` — built-in fake timer isolation without Jest/Vitest  [official]

Node.js 20+ `node:test` exposes `context.mock.timers` for fake timer control within a single test context. Timers are automatically restored when the test ends — there is no explicit `useRealTimers()` teardown required, making accidental timer leaks structurally impossible.

```typescript
// tests/scheduler.test.ts
import { describe, it } from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { JobScheduler } from '../src/scheduler.js';

describe('JobScheduler', () => {
  it('executes a job after the scheduled delay', (t) => {
    // t.mock.timers is auto-restored when this test completes
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout', 'Date'] });
    t.mock.timers.setTime(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0));

    const scheduler = new JobScheduler();
    const job = t.mock.fn<() => void>();

    scheduler.schedule(job, 5000);
    t.mock.timers.tick(5000);

    assert.strictEqual(job.mock.calls.length, 1);
  });

  it('does not execute a job before the delay elapses', (t) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout'] });

    const scheduler = new JobScheduler();
    const job = t.mock.fn<() => void>();

    scheduler.schedule(job, 10000);
    t.mock.timers.tick(9999);

    assert.strictEqual(job.mock.calls.length, 0);
    // node:test auto-restores timers — next test gets real setTimeout
  });

  it('cancels a scheduled job when abort() is called', (t) => {
    t.mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['setTimeout'] });

    const scheduler = new JobScheduler();
    const job = t.mock.fn<() => void>();

    scheduler.schedule(job, 5000);
    scheduler.cancel(job);
    t.mock.timers.tick(10000); // Advance past scheduled time

    assert.strictEqual(job.mock.calls.length, 0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: adopting `node:test` as the test runner to reduce external dependencies (Node 20+ only). Do NOT use if the production code under test uses `queueMicrotask` or `Promise` chains dependent on microtask ordering — `t.mock.timers` controls macrotask timers only, not the microtask queue. Alternative: Jest `useFakeTimers()` or Vitest `vi.useFakeTimers()` for richer fake timer control including `Promise.resolve()` microtask advancement. [official]

---

### Pattern 149: Playwright `test.step()` with `{ box: true }` — opaque isolation of sub-steps in error traces  [official]

Playwright `test.step(title, fn, { box: true })` marks a step as a "box" — when the step fails, the error is attributed to the step call site rather than the internal line. This isolates fixture helper logic from test error traces, preventing test-helper implementation details from appearing in failure reports and polluting stack-trace-based debugging.

```typescript
// tests/helpers/formHelper.ts
import { type Page, test } from '@playwright/test';

export async function fillRegistrationForm(
  page: Page,
  data: { name: string; email: string; password: string }
): Promise<void> {
  // { box: true } — failure reported as "fillRegistrationForm failed",
  // not the internal page.fill() line number
  await test.step('fill registration form', async () => {
    await page.locator('[name="fullName"]').fill(data.name);
    await page.locator('[name="email"]').fill(data.email);
    await page.locator('[name="password"]').fill(data.password);
    await page.locator('[name="confirmPassword"]').fill(data.password);
    await page.locator('button[type="submit"]').click();
  }, { box: true });
}

// tests/registration.spec.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { fillRegistrationForm } from './helpers/formHelper';

test.describe('user registration', () => {
  test('successfully registers with valid data', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    await fillRegistrationForm(page, {
      name: 'Dana Lee',
      email: 'dana@example.com',
      password: 'S3cur3P@ss!',
    });

    await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="welcome-msg"]')).toContainText('Dana Lee');
  });

  test('shows error for duplicate email', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/register');

    await fillRegistrationForm(page, {
      name: 'Existing User',
      email: 'existing@example.com',
      password: 'P@ssword1',
    });

    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="email-error"]')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="email-error"]')).toContainText('already registered');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: helper functions perform multiple page interactions and you want failures to surface at the helper call site, not deep inside helper internals. Do NOT overuse `{ box: true }` on trivial single-action helpers — the boxing adds overhead and may hide genuinely useful internal line information. Alternative: omit `{ box: true }` when you want full internal trace visibility during active development. [official]

---

### Pattern 150: Jest `defineConfig` + `mergeConfig` type-safe composition — isolation config inheritance without `Config` type cast  [official]

Jest 30 exports `defineConfig()` and `mergeConfig()` helpers (analogous to Vitest's) enabling type-safe config composition. Base isolation settings (mock reset, worker limits, coverage) are defined once and merged into project-specific configs without losing TypeScript inference.

```typescript
// jest.config.base.ts — shared isolation baseline
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export const baseConfig = defineConfig({
  // Universal isolation settings
  clearMocks: true,
  restoreMocks: true,
  resetModules: false, // Opt-in per project — not global default
  testEnvironment: 'node',
  // Prevent workers from exceeding connection pool size in integration suites
  maxWorkers: '50%',
  workerIdleMemoryLimit: '512MB',
});

// jest.config.unit.ts — unit test project
import { defineConfig, mergeConfig } from 'jest';
import { baseConfig } from './jest.config.base';

export default mergeConfig(
  baseConfig,
  defineConfig({
    displayName: 'unit',
    testMatch: ['<rootDir>/src/**/*.test.ts'],
    // Unit tests reset modules per-test for singleton isolation
    resetModules: true,
  })
);

// jest.config.integration.ts — integration test project
import { defineConfig, mergeConfig } from 'jest';
import { baseConfig } from './jest.config.base';

export default mergeConfig(
  baseConfig,
  defineConfig({
    displayName: 'integration',
    testMatch: ['<rootDir>/tests/integration/**/*.test.ts'],
    testEnvironment: 'node',
    // Limit parallelism for DB connection pool safety
    maxWorkers: 2,
    globalSetup: '<rootDir>/tests/integration/globalSetup.ts',
    globalTeardown: '<rootDir>/tests/integration/globalTeardown.ts',
  })
);
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: a monorepo or multi-project repo needs shared isolation settings without copy-paste drift between configs. Do NOT use `mergeConfig` to silently override critical settings like `testEnvironment` from the base — make overrides explicit and document why each override is needed. Alternative: Jest `projects` array in a single root config achieves the same multi-project structure but is less composable when config files grow large. [official]

---

### Pattern 151: `vi.mockObject()` with `spy` option — automatic spy wrapping for entire object interfaces  [official]

Vitest 3.2+ `vi.mockObject(target, { spy: true })` creates a spy-wrapped copy of every method on the target object, preserving the original implementations by default. This replaces the verbose pattern of calling `vi.spyOn()` on each method individually and is safely reset via `vi.restoreAllMocks()`.

```typescript
// src/notificationService.ts
export const notificationService = {
  async sendEmail(to: string, subject: string, body: string): Promise<void> {
    throw new Error('notificationService.sendEmail must not be called in tests');
  },
  async sendSMS(to: string, message: string): Promise<void> {
    throw new Error('notificationService.sendSMS must not be called in tests');
  },
  async sendPush(deviceToken: string, payload: object): Promise<void> {
    throw new Error('notificationService.sendPush must not be called in tests');
  },
};

// tests/orderService.test.ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import { notificationService } from '../src/notificationService';
import { placeOrder } from '../src/orderService';

describe('placeOrder', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    // Wrap ALL methods as spies with no-op implementations
    vi.mockObject(notificationService, { spy: true });
    vi.spyOn(notificationService, 'sendEmail').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    vi.spyOn(notificationService, 'sendSMS').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    vi.spyOn(notificationService, 'sendPush').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
  });

  afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks());

  it('sends an email confirmation when order is placed', async () => {
    await placeOrder({ userId: 'u1', items: [{ sku: 'ABC', qty: 2 }] });

    expect(notificationService.sendEmail).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(notificationService.sendEmail).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.stringContaining('@'),
      'Order Confirmation',
      expect.stringContaining('ABC')
    );
  });

  it('does not send SMS for standard orders', async () => {
    await placeOrder({ userId: 'u1', items: [{ sku: 'ABC', qty: 1 }] });
    expect(notificationService.sendSMS).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('does not send push notification for standard orders', async () => {
    await placeOrder({ userId: 'u1', items: [{ sku: 'XYZ', qty: 1 }] });
    expect(notificationService.sendPush).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: you need to spy on multiple methods of a service object without tediously calling `vi.spyOn()` on each one. Do NOT use `vi.mockObject` as a replacement for full module mocking (`vi.mock()`) — `vi.mockObject` wraps an existing object reference, it does not intercept module import resolution. Alternative: `vi.mock()` with a factory that returns an object of `vi.fn()` values, when import-level interception is also required. [official]
