### Pattern 178: Jest `clearMocks` / `resetMocks` / `restoreMocks` decision table — choosing the right automatic mock cleanup level  [official]

The three Jest mock-cleanup flags operate at different levels. The common mistake is using only `clearMocks: true` and assuming implementations are reset between tests — they are not.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export default defineConfig({
  testEnvironment: 'node',
  // restoreMocks: true is the superset — clears + resets + restores.
  // Use this unless you have a specific reason to keep implementations.
  restoreMocks: true,
});

// tests/notification.test.ts
// Demonstration of what each cleanup level does:
//
// clearMocks: true
//   - Resets call count, call args, return values recorded on the mock
//   - Does NOT remove the mock implementation (mockReturnValue persists)
//   - Does NOT restore spied methods to originals
//
// resetMocks: true (superset of clearMocks)
//   - Resets call history AND removes mock implementation
//   - jest.spyOn() still wraps the method — it returns undefined (no impl)
//   - Does NOT restore spied methods to originals
//
// restoreMocks: true (superset of resetMocks)
//   - Resets call history, removes implementation, AND restores original
//   - jest.spyOn() spy is fully removed; original method active again
//   - Safe default for suites using jest.spyOn() throughout

import { describe, test, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import * as mailer from '../src/mailer';

describe('restoreMocks demonstration', () => {
  test('spy is fresh — no bleed from previous test', () => {
    // restoreMocks:true means the previous test's spy was removed
    const spy = jest.spyOn(mailer, 'send').mockResolvedValue(undefined);
    mailer.send({ to: 'a@b.com', subject: 'Hi', body: 'Hello' });
    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });

  test('spy from previous test is gone — original mailer.send is active', () => {
    // Without restoreMocks, the spy from the previous test would still be here
    expect(jest.isMockFunction(mailer.send)).toBe(false);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `restoreMocks: true` as the default — it is the safest superset. Only drop to `clearMocks: true` if you have module-level `jest.spyOn()` calls (outside `beforeEach`) whose implementation you intentionally share across all tests in the file. Named alternative: manually call `jest.restoreAllMocks()` in `afterEach` for per-file control without global config. [official]

---

### Pattern 179: Vitest `aroundEach` wrapping pattern — single try/finally for guaranteed database transaction rollback  [official]

`aroundEach(fn)` passes a `next()` function that runs the test body. Code before `next()` is setup; code after (or in `finally`) is teardown. Unlike `beforeEach`/`afterEach` pairs, `aroundEach` keeps setup and teardown in one closure, ensuring teardown runs even when a test throws before `afterEach` would normally fire.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';
export default defineConfig({ test: { globals: true } });

// tests/user-repo.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { pool } from '../src/db';
import { UserRepository } from '../src/userRepository';
import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';

describe('UserRepository — aroundEach rollback isolation', () => {
  let client: PoolClient;

  // aroundEach is a Vitest 4.1 global (requires globals:true)
  // @ts-expect-error aroundEach is injected by Vitest when globals:true
  aroundEach(async (next) => {
    client = await pool.connect();
    await client.query('BEGIN');
    try {
      await next(); // run the test body
    } finally {
      // Guaranteed rollback — runs even if next() throws
      await client.query('ROLLBACK');
      client.release();
    }
  });

  test('persists a user within the rolled-back transaction', async () => {
    const repo = new UserRepository(client);
    const user = await repo.create({ name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@test.invalid' });
    expect(user.id).toBeDefined();
    expect(user.name).toBe('Alice');
  });

  test('does not see the previous test user — transaction was rolled back', async () => {
    const repo = new UserRepository(client);
    const users = await repo.findAll();
    const alice = users.find((u) => u.email === 'alice@test.invalid');
    expect(alice).toBeUndefined();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: integration tests must use real database rows within a test but must not commit them. Do NOT use `aroundEach` for connection pool tests where opening/closing connections is the behaviour under test — the injected client hides that. Named alternative: Testcontainers per-suite Docker isolation (Pattern 44) when transactions are insufficient (e.g., DDL operations that cannot be rolled back). [official]

---

### Pattern 180: Playwright `test.fail()` — expected-failure isolation to prevent false greens masking real regressions  [official]

`test.fail()` marks a test that is expected to fail. If the test unexpectedly passes, Playwright reports it as a failure — providing an automated signal when a known bug is fixed and the annotation can be removed.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Known regression: payment provider returns 500 on Amex cards in staging.
// Bug: PW-2341 — expected to be fixed in Sprint 24.
// When fixed, Playwright will report: "Expected to fail but passed" — remove .fail() then.
test.fail(
  'processes Amex card successfully',
  async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.fill('[data-testid=card-number]', '378282246310005');
    await page.fill('[data-testid=card-expiry]', '12/26');
    await page.fill('[data-testid=card-cvv]', '1234');
    await page.click('[data-testid=pay-button]');

    // This assertion currently fails (server returns 500)
    await expect(page.getByText('Payment successful')).toBeVisible({
      timeout: 5000,
    });
  }
);

test('processes Visa card successfully', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.fill('[data-testid=card-number]', '4242424242424242');
  await page.fill('[data-testid=card-expiry]', '12/26');
  await page.fill('[data-testid=card-cvv]', '123');
  await page.click('[data-testid=pay-button]');
  await expect(page.getByText('Payment successful')).toBeVisible();
});

// Conditional .fail() for environment-specific known failures
test.fail(
  process.env.CI_ENVIRONMENT === 'staging',
  'loads within 2s on staging (known slow cold-start)',
  async ({ page }) => {
    const start = Date.now();
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    expect(Date.now() - start).toBeLessThan(2000);
  }
);
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when: a test must remain in the suite while a bug is being fixed, and you want an automated signal when the fix lands. Do NOT use `test.fail()` as a long-term state — set a sprint deadline comment and treat unexpected passes as a priority to remove the annotation. Named alternative: `test.fixme()` conveys intent more clearly in reports but behaves identically to `test.fail()`. [official]

## Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 30

190. **Vitest `onCleanup` silently ignores the second call — teardown for the second resource never runs, causing connection leaks in CI.** [community]
    WHY: `onCleanup` registers exactly one cleanup callback per fixture. When a fixture calls `onCleanup(() => db.disconnect())` then `onCleanup(() => queue.stop())`, only the first registration is honoured. The queue is never stopped. Because queue workers hold the event loop open, Vitest's `detectAsyncLeaks` reports "open handles after test" in the next test — which is the first visible symptom. The root cause is in the fixture, not the leaked test. Fix: fuse all teardown into one callback as shown in Pattern 166.

191. **Jest `fakeTimers.doNotFake` is ignored when `enableGlobally: false` — the array has no effect unless global fake timers are active.** [community]
    WHY: `doNotFake` is an exclusion list applied to the globally-enabled fake timer set. When `enableGlobally` is `false` (the default), no timer API is faked at the global level, so the exclusion list is vacuous. Developers who set `doNotFake: ['Date']` expecting it to prevent Date faking in individual `jest.useFakeTimers()` calls are mistaken — `doNotFake` only applies to the global `fakeTimers` config block, not per-test invocations. For per-test control, pass `{ doNotFake: ['Date'] }` as an argument to `jest.useFakeTimers({ doNotFake: ['Date'] })` instead.

192. **Playwright `page.route()` with a glob pattern does not override a previously registered `context.route()` for the same URL — both handlers fire in registration order.** [community]
    WHY: `page.route()` appends a handler to the route stack. A `context.route()` registered in a higher-scoped fixture is also on the stack. If the context-level handler calls `route.continue()`, the page-level handler also fires, producing double interceptions and unexpected responses when the test's `route.fulfill()` runs after the fixture's conditional `route.abort()`. Fix: call `page.unroute(pattern)` before re-registering the route in a test, or design fixtures to use `route.continue()` exclusively so test-level handlers can fully override them.

193. **`jest.resetModules()` in `beforeEach` does NOT unmock modules registered with `jest.mock()` at the file top level — the automock factory persists across resets.** [community]
    WHY: `jest.resetModules()` clears the module registry cache so that subsequent `require`/`import` calls re-evaluate the module file. It does NOT clear the manual mock registry maintained by `jest.mock()`. So after `jest.resetModules()`, calling `require('../src/userService')` re-evaluates the module, but the factory registered by `jest.mock('../src/userService', factory)` is still active. To load the real module after a `jest.mock()` registration, you must call `jest.unmock('../src/userService')` in addition to `jest.resetModules()`.

194. **Vitest `scope: 'file'` fixtures are NOT re-created between `describe` blocks in the same file — mutations in one `describe`'s tests contaminate the next.** [community]
    WHY: File-scoped fixtures are created once when the first test in the file accesses them and destroyed when the last test in the file completes. Two `describe` blocks in the same file sharing a file-scoped `db` fixture share the same database client instance. If the first `describe`'s test mutates connection state (e.g., sets a transaction isolation level or changes the search path), the second `describe` inherits that state. Use `scope: 'test'` for any fixture whose state must be isolated per-describe. File scope is safe only for genuinely read-only resources.

195. **MSW `{ once: true }` handler leaves a consumed-but-not-removed entry in the stack that allows subsequent matching requests to fall through to the real network — `onUnhandledRequest: 'error'` does NOT catch this.** [community]
    WHY: A once handler intercepts its first matching request, fires the response, and marks itself as consumed. On subsequent matching requests the consumed entry is still in the stack; MSW iterates, finds it, but skips it. If no other handler matches, the request falls through to the real network. Because an entry did match (even though consumed), MSW does not classify the request as "unhandled" — `onUnhandledRequest: 'error'` does not fire. The real network call silently leaks. Fix: `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` unconditionally removes all once handlers whether consumed or not.

196. **Node.js `--test-global-setup` runs in the same process as test workers when `isolation: 'none'` — module-level singletons created in globalSetup are shared directly with all tests and cannot be reset between them.** [community]
    WHY: Unlike Jest's `globalSetup` (which runs in a separate subprocess), Node.js `--test-global-setup` executes in the same process when `isolation: 'none'` is specified for speed. Any object exported from the setup module is the same reference used by every test. There is no `jest.resetModules()` equivalent in `node:test`. Fix: use `isolation: 'process'` (the default) if globalSetup must provide singletons that tests should not share, or design globalSetup to only return serialisable data that each test reconstructs locally.

197. **Playwright `fullyParallel: true` with a `serial` describe in one file does not prevent a sibling default-mode describe from racing against the serial block's setup state.** [community]
    WHY: `fullyParallel` distributes individual tests to workers. `serial` mode makes a describe block atomic — its tests run sequentially in one worker. But a sibling describe with `beforeAll` in the same file is scheduled independently and may start before, during, or after the serial block. If `beforeAll` in the sibling mutates shared application state (e.g., seeds a table), and the serial block's first test reads that table before the seed completes, it sees stale data. Fix: apply `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` at the file's outermost scope, or separate conflicting suites into different files.

198. **Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` reports a false positive for a `setInterval` started in `beforeAll` and cleared in `afterAll` — the interval is active during tests and Vitest counts it as leaked.** [community]
    WHY: `detectAsyncLeaks` inspects the Node.js async resource tree after each individual test completes, not after the full suite. An interval started in `beforeAll` and cleared in `afterAll` is correctly bounded at the suite level, but it is open during every individual test. Vitest sees it as an open handle and reports it as a leak, producing spurious warnings for correctly-managed suite-level timers. Fix: move the interval into a Vitest fixture with `onCleanup` so it is created and destroyed around each test, or validate the warning is a false positive by replacing `setInterval` with `vi.fn()` temporarily.

199. **Jest `workerIdleMemoryLimit` recycles the worker at idle time — if a previous test file spiked RSS beyond the limit, the worker is replaced at the next idle point and `afterAll` teardown from that spike file runs in a new worker where `beforeAll`-created resources do not exist.** [community]
    WHY: `workerIdleMemoryLimit` is checked between test files (at worker idle). If a file causes RSS to spike past the limit, the worker is recycled before the next file. The next file's `afterAll` runs in the replacement worker, but resources allocated in the spike file's `beforeAll` (e.g., a database connection stored in a module-level variable) no longer exist in the new worker. `afterAll` teardown silently no-ops. Fix: set the memory limit high enough for peak RSS, and add `--forceExit` as a backstop for workers that fail to release resources before Jest process exit.

## Quick Reference — Cycle 30

| Problem | Symptom | Solution | Framework |
|---------|---------|----------|-----------|
| `onCleanup` called twice in fixture | Second resource never cleaned; async leak in next test | Fuse all teardown into one `onCleanup` callback | Vitest |
| `fakeTimers.doNotFake` has no effect | `Date` still faked despite exclusion | Only effective with `enableGlobally: true`; per-test: pass option to `jest.useFakeTimers()` | Jest |
| `page.route()` not overriding context-level route | Both handlers fire; double interception | Call `page.unroute(pattern)` before re-registering | Playwright |
| `jest.resetModules()` does not remove `jest.mock()` factory | Real module still not loaded after reset | Add `jest.unmock()` alongside `jest.resetModules()` | Jest |
| File-scoped Vitest fixture mutated across `describe` blocks | Second describe sees stale/dirty state | Use `scope: 'test'` for stateful fixtures | Vitest |
| MSW `once: true` leaks to real network after handler fires | Silent real network call; `onUnhandledRequest` not triggered | Use `server.resetHandlers()` in `afterEach` | MSW v2 |
| `--test-global-setup` singleton shared when `isolation: 'none'` | `beforeEach` resets have no effect on shared object | Use `isolation: 'process'` or return only serialisable data | Node.js |
| `fullyParallel` sibling `beforeAll` races serial describe | Stale data reads; intermittent failures | Separate conflicting suites into different files | Playwright |
| `detectAsyncLeaks` false positive for `beforeAll` interval | Spurious open-handle warning | Move timer into fixture with `onCleanup` | Vitest |
| `workerIdleMemoryLimit` recycles worker; `afterAll` no-ops | Teardown runs in wrong worker, resources leak | Set limit above peak RSS; add `--forceExit` backstop | Jest |
| Auth re-run per test slows CI significantly | Login flow executed for every test | Use worker-scoped `storageState` fixture (Pattern 172) | Playwright |
| ESM mock from one test bleeds into next test | Mock implementation active after test | `jest.resetModules()` + `jest.unstable_mockModule()` + dynamic import | Jest |
| `vi.stubEnv` not automatically restored | Next test sees previous test's env value | Enable `unstubEnvs: true` in vitest.config.ts | Vitest |

### Pattern 181: Jest 30 `globalsCleanup: 'on'` — automatic VM global leak prevention between test files  [official]

Jest 30 introduced `globalsCleanup` in `testEnvironmentOptions` to address memory leaks and cross-file state contamination caused by test code that mutates `globalThis` or stores references in the global VM context. With `'on'`, Jest automatically wipes unprotected globals after each test file. With `'soft'` (the default), it only warns. With `'off'`, the pre-Jest-30 behaviour is preserved.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export default defineConfig({
  testEnvironment: 'node',
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    // 'on': automatically clean globals after each file
    // 'soft': warn about uncleaned globals (default)
    // 'off': legacy no-cleanup behaviour
    globalsCleanup: 'on',
  },
});

// tests/analytics.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from '@jest/globals';

// Bad pattern this catches: attaching a module-level cache to globalThis
// globalThis.__analyticsCache = {};  <-- survives to the next test file without globalsCleanup

describe('analytics global cleanup', () => {
  test('registers a global analytics tracker', () => {
    (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__analyticsQueue = [];
    (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__analyticsQueue = [
      ...(globalThis.__analyticsQueue as unknown[]),
      { event: 'pageview', path: '/home' },
    ];
    expect((globalThis.__analyticsQueue as unknown[]).length).toBe(1);
  });

  test('tracker is still present within the same file', () => {
    // Within the same file, the global is not cleaned yet
    expect(globalThis.__analyticsQueue).toBeDefined();
  });
});
// After this file completes, globalsCleanup:'on' wipes __analyticsQueue
// so the next test file starts with a clean globalThis
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `'on'` for any project where test files interact with `globalThis`, browser-like globals (injected via `jsdom`), or singleton caches attached to the global scope. Do NOT use `'on'` if legacy setup files intentionally share mutable global state across test files by design — those will be wiped unexpectedly. Named alternative: `protectProperties(globalThis['my-property'])` from `jest-util` to exempt specific globals from cleanup while enabling `'on'` for everything else. [official]

### Pattern 182: Vitest `test.override` — per-suite fixture value replacement without global pollution  [official]

`test.override` (Vitest 4.1, replacing deprecated `test.scoped`) allows overriding a fixture's value for all tests in a specific describe block without modifying the fixture implementation or creating a new fixture. The override is scoped precisely to the suite and does not leak to sibling or parent describes.

```typescript
// fixtures/db.ts
import { test as base } from 'vitest';

interface DbFixtures {
  dbUrl: string;
  timeout: number;
}

export const test = base.extend<DbFixtures>({
  dbUrl: async ({}, use) => {
    // Default: use shared test database
    await use(process.env.TEST_DB_URL ?? 'postgres://localhost:5432/testdb');
  },
  timeout: async ({}, use) => {
    await use(5000); // default 5s query timeout
  },
});

// tests/slow-migrations.test.ts
import { describe, expect } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '../fixtures/db';
import { runMigration } from '../src/migrations';

// Override timeout for the entire slow-migrations suite only
describe('slow migrations', () => {
  // test.override replaces 'timeout' for every test in this describe
  test.override({ timeout: 60_000 });

  test('runs the backfill migration without timing out', async ({ dbUrl, timeout }) => {
    // timeout === 60_000 here — the override is active
    const result = await runMigration('backfill_user_metadata', {
      connectionString: dbUrl,
      statementTimeout: timeout,
    });
    expect(result.rowsAffected).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });

  test('runs the index migration within the extended timeout', async ({ dbUrl, timeout }) => {
    expect(timeout).toBe(60_000); // confirmed: override applies to this test too
    const result = await runMigration('create_idx_user_email', {
      connectionString: dbUrl,
      statementTimeout: timeout,
    });
    expect(result.success).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe('fast queries', () => {
  test('reads a user record with default timeout', async ({ timeout }) => {
    // timeout === 5000 here — the override does NOT leak out of the sibling describe
    expect(timeout).toBe(5000);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use when a subset of tests in a file needs a different fixture value (e.g., extended timeout, alternative endpoint, staging credentials) without creating a separate fixture file. Do NOT use `test.override` to change fixture values that affect global singletons — the override is scoped but the singleton mutation is not. Named alternative: create a separate `slowTest` fixture that extends the base `test` with the modified value, which is more explicit and re-usable across files. [official]

### Pattern 183: Jest `retryTimes` with `retryImmediately: true` — immediate retry without queuing delay for transient-failure isolation  [official]

`jest.retryTimes(n, { retryImmediately: true })` retries a flaky test immediately in the same worker, bypassing the normal queue scheduling delay. This is distinct from the default behaviour where a retried test waits for other tests to complete first, which can change the timing context and make timing-sensitive flakiness harder to reproduce.

```typescript
// tests/cache-invalidation.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { CacheService } from '../src/cacheService';
import { sleep } from '../src/utils';

// Retry up to 3 times immediately — do not wait for other tests between attempts.
// Use for tests that fail transiently due to race conditions in async code,
// not as a substitute for proper isolation.
jest.retryTimes(3, { retryImmediately: true });

describe('CacheService TTL expiry', () => {
  let cache: CacheService;

  beforeEach(() => {
    cache = new CacheService({ defaultTtlMs: 100 });
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await cache.destroy();
  });

  test('entry is absent after TTL expires', async () => {
    cache.set('key', 'value');
    // Wait slightly longer than TTL — CI timing jitter can make this flaky
    await sleep(120);
    const result = cache.get('key');
    expect(result).toBeNull();
  });

  test('fresh entry is present before TTL expires', async () => {
    cache.set('fresh', 'data');
    await sleep(50); // well before TTL
    expect(cache.get('fresh')).toBe('data');
  });

  test('TTL resets on re-set', async () => {
    cache.set('key', 'v1');
    await sleep(60);
    cache.set('key', 'v2'); // resets TTL
    await sleep(60);         // total 120ms but re-set was at 60ms — should still be present
    expect(cache.get('key')).toBe('v2');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `retryImmediately: true` for inherently timing-dependent tests (cache TTLs, debounce delays, rate-limit windows) where retry delay would invalidate the test context. Do NOT use retries as a substitute for fixing flaky isolation — a test that needs more than 1 retry is telling you the timing assumption is wrong. Named alternative: use `jest.useFakeTimers()` and `jest.advanceTimersByTime()` to eliminate real-time dependency entirely; prefer fake timers when the timer source is within your control. [official]

### Pattern 184: Playwright `page.clock.install` before navigation — deterministic time isolation for time-dependent UI flows  [official]

`page.clock.install({ time })` installs a fake clock before the page loads, ensuring that `Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, and `performance.now()` are all replaced with controllable fakes from the first moment of page execution. This prevents timing races where the real clock advances between test setup and the first page render.

```typescript
// tests/session-timeout.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('shows session expiry warning after 29 minutes of inactivity', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install fake clock BEFORE navigation — this ensures the clock is fixed
  // when the page's own scripts first run and register their timers.
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-15T09:00:00Z') });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Verify initial state — no warning yet
  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).not.toBeVisible();

  // Advance the fake clock by 29 minutes — triggers the warning timer
  await page.clock.fastForward('29:00');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).toContainText(
    'Your session will expire in 1 minute'
  );

  // Advance 1 more minute — triggers session expiry redirect
  await page.clock.fastForward('01:00');

  await expect(page).toHaveURL('/login?reason=session_expired');
});

test('session warning is dismissed by user activity — timer resets', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-15T09:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Advance 29 minutes to trigger warning
  await page.clock.fastForward('29:00');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).toBeVisible();

  // Simulate user activity — warning dismisses and timer resets
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).not.toBeVisible();

  // 29 more minutes — should warn again (timer reset from user activity)
  await page.clock.fastForward('29:00');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('session-warning')).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `page.clock.install` before navigation for any test involving timers, session expiry, countdowns, or date-dependent UI. Do NOT install the clock after navigation if the page sets up timers in its initialization scripts — the real clock will have already run those timers and the fake clock cannot retroactively intercept them. Named alternative: `page.addInitScript(() => { Date.now = () => 1705312800000; })` for Date-only isolation, but this does not fake `setTimeout`/`setInterval`. [official]

### Pattern 185: Vitest `viteModuleRunner: false` — production-faithful module evaluation for catching sandbox-invisible isolation bugs  [official]

Setting `viteModuleRunner: false` in a Vitest project configuration disables the Vite module sandbox and runs tests with native Node.js `require`/`import` semantics. This catches bugs that are invisible under Vite's sandbox — such as modules that rely on `__dirname` injection, path alias assumptions, or ESM/CJS interop differences that Vite silently normalises.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    // Run most tests with the Vite sandbox for speed and DX
    pool: 'forks',

    projects: [
      {
        // Primary suite: sandboxed Vite module runner (fast, permissive)
        test: {
          name: 'sandboxed',
          include: ['src/**/*.test.ts'],
          environment: 'node',
        },
      },
      {
        // Strict suite: native Node.js module evaluation (catches sandbox-invisible bugs)
        test: {
          name: 'strict-esm',
          include: ['src/esm-boundary/**/*.test.ts'],
          environment: 'node',
          // Disable Vite module runner — use native Node.js import()
          // This will surface __dirname, path.resolve, and ESM/CJS interop issues
          // that Vite's sandbox silently papers over.
          // @ts-expect-error: experimental option
          viteModuleRunner: false,
        },
      },
    ],
  },
});

// src/esm-boundary/loader.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { loadPlugin } from '../loader';

describe('plugin loader — native ESM evaluation', () => {
  test('resolves plugin path relative to caller file, not process.cwd()', async () => {
    // Under viteModuleRunner:false, __dirname is the real file system path.
    // Under the Vite sandbox, __dirname is injected and may differ — masking real bugs.
    const plugin = await loadPlugin('./fixtures/echo-plugin');
    expect(plugin.name).toBe('echo');
  });

  test('throws on missing default export — not silently undefined', async () => {
    // Vite sandbox sometimes returns undefined for missing named ESM exports;
    // native Node.js throws ReferenceError — the production behaviour.
    await expect(loadPlugin('./fixtures/no-default')).rejects.toThrow();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `viteModuleRunner: false` for tests of module loading logic, plugin systems, dynamic `import()` paths, and ESM/CJS boundary code that will run in production Node.js without Vite. Do NOT apply it to all tests — it disables Vite's HMR-friendly module graph and significantly increases test startup time. Named alternative: run a dedicated `node --experimental-vm-modules jest` suite alongside Vitest for maximum ESM fidelity without Vitest's experimental flag. [official]

### Pattern 186: Jest `globalsCleanup` + `protectProperties` — exempting intentional shared globals from automatic cleanup  [official]

When `globalsCleanup: 'on'` is enabled, Jest wipes all non-protected globals after each test file. Use `protectProperties` from `jest-util` to exempt specific globals that are genuinely designed for cross-file sharing — such as a test server URL or a shared database connection string computed once during global setup.

```typescript
// jest.globalSetup.ts
import { protectProperties } from 'jest-util';

export default async function globalSetup(): Promise<void> {
  // Start a real HTTP server once for the entire test run
  const { createTestServer } = await import('./tests/helpers/testServer');
  const server = await createTestServer();
  const port = (server.address() as { port: number }).port;

  // Attach to globalThis so all test files can read it
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testServerPort = port;
  (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testServerTeardown = () =>
    new Promise<void>((resolve) => server.close(() => resolve()));

  // Protect these globals from globalsCleanup: 'on' wiping them
  // after the first test file completes.
  protectProperties(globalThis, ['__testServerPort', '__testServerTeardown']);
}

// jest.globalTeardown.ts
export default async function globalTeardown(): Promise<void> {
  const teardown = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>)
    .__testServerTeardown as () => Promise<void>;
  if (teardown) {
    await teardown();
  }
}

// jest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export default defineConfig({
  globalSetup: './jest.globalSetup.ts',
  globalTeardown: './jest.globalTeardown.ts',
  testEnvironmentOptions: {
    globalsCleanup: 'on', // wipe everything EXCEPT protected globals
  },
});

// tests/api.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from '@jest/globals';

describe('API endpoint isolation', () => {
  test('connects to the shared test server', async () => {
    const port = (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__testServerPort as number;
    const res = await fetch(`http://localhost:${port}/health`);
    expect(res.status).toBe(200);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `protectProperties` for read-only cross-test-file globals that are expensive to recreate (server ports, shared DB URLs, test certificates). Do NOT protect mutable globals — the protection prevents cleanup but does not provide isolation, so any test that mutates the protected global contaminates subsequent files. Named alternative: store cross-file setup output in a temporary file (e.g., `jest-e2e-config.json`) and read it in each test file — avoids global mutation entirely. [official]

### Pattern 187: Vitest `aroundAll` with fixture context — guaranteed suite-level database seeding and teardown  [official]

`aroundAll` (Vitest 4.1) wraps an entire describe suite, similar to `aroundEach` but spanning the whole block. The callback receives a fixture context, allowing it to access file-scoped or worker-scoped fixtures for setup operations that must run once before all tests in the suite and clean up after all of them.

```typescript
// fixtures/db.ts
import { test as base } from 'vitest';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

interface DbFixtures {
  pool: Pool;
  schemaName: string;
}

export const test = base.extend<DbFixtures>({
  pool: [
    async ({}, use) => {
      const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.TEST_DB_URL });
      await use(pool);
      await pool.end();
    },
    { scope: 'file' }, // shared across all tests in the file
  ],
  schemaName: [
    async ({}, use) => {
      // Each worker gets its own schema to prevent parallel conflicts
      const name = `test_${process.env.VITEST_WORKER_ID ?? '0'}`;
      await use(name);
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

// tests/invoice-suite.test.ts
import { describe, expect } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '../fixtures/db';
import { seedInvoices, clearInvoices, fetchInvoices } from '../src/invoiceRepository';

describe('invoice repository — seeded suite', () => {
  // aroundAll receives fixture context in Vitest 4.1+
  // Setup runs before ANY test; teardown runs after ALL tests
  test.extend({}).aroundAll?.(async (suite, { pool, schemaName }) => {
    await pool.query(`SET search_path TO ${schemaName}`);
    await seedInvoices(pool, [
      { id: 'inv-1', amount: 100, status: 'paid' },
      { id: 'inv-2', amount: 200, status: 'pending' },
      { id: 'inv-3', amount: 150, status: 'overdue' },
    ]);
    await suite(); // run all tests
    await clearInvoices(pool); // guaranteed cleanup
  });

  test('returns all seeded invoices', async ({ pool }) => {
    const invoices = await fetchInvoices(pool);
    expect(invoices).toHaveLength(3);
  });

  test('filters paid invoices correctly', async ({ pool }) => {
    const paid = await fetchInvoices(pool, { status: 'paid' });
    expect(paid).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(paid[0].id).toBe('inv-1');
  });

  test('filters overdue invoices correctly', async ({ pool }) => {
    const overdue = await fetchInvoices(pool, { status: 'overdue' });
    expect(overdue).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(overdue[0].amount).toBe(150);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `aroundAll` when a suite shares a read-only (or carefully controlled) dataset that is expensive to seed per-test but must be cleaned up when the suite exits. Do NOT use `aroundAll` if any test in the suite mutates the seeded data — use `aroundEach` with per-test transactions (Pattern 179) instead. Named alternative: `beforeAll` + `afterAll` pair achieves the same setup/teardown but does not guarantee teardown runs when a test throws and crashes the worker before `afterAll` executes. [official]

### Pattern 188: Jest `maxConcurrency` cap for `test.concurrent` — preventing resource exhaustion in parallel integration tests  [official]

`maxConcurrency` (Jest config) limits how many concurrent tests from `test.concurrent` suites can run simultaneously in a single worker. Without a cap, a describe with many `test.concurrent` cases can saturate database connection pools, file descriptor limits, or network socket limits, causing flaky resource-exhaustion failures in CI.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export default defineConfig({
  // Limit concurrent tests per worker to 5
  // This prevents a burst of 50 concurrent tests from exhausting the DB pool
  maxConcurrency: 5,
  testEnvironment: 'node',
});

// tests/user-api.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from '@jest/globals';
import { createUser, getUser, deleteUser } from '../src/userApi';

// These tests run concurrently — up to maxConcurrency (5) at a time
describe('user API concurrent isolation', () => {
  // Each concurrent test must use a unique resource identifier
  // to prevent cross-test interference
  const workers = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => i);

  test.each(workers)(
    'creates and retrieves user %i without cross-contamination',
    async (workerIndex) => {
      const email = `user-concurrent-${workerIndex}@test.invalid`;
      const created = await createUser({ email, name: `Worker ${workerIndex}` });

      try {
        const fetched = await getUser(created.id);
        expect(fetched.email).toBe(email);
        // Verify no cross-contamination: name must match THIS worker's data
        expect(fetched.name).toBe(`Worker ${workerIndex}`);
      } finally {
        // Cleanup even on failure — isolation requires each test cleans its own state
        await deleteUser(created.id);
      }
    }
  );
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `maxConcurrency` when integration tests use `test.concurrent` and share finite resources (DB pools, file handles, external API rate limits). Start with `5` and tune upward based on observed resource utilisation. Do NOT set `maxConcurrency` to `1` — that effectively serialises concurrent tests and defeats their purpose; use `describe` without `.concurrent` instead. Named alternative: Testcontainers with a pool of containers sized to `maxConcurrency` (Pattern 93) when each concurrent test requires complete database isolation, not just connection limiting. [official]

---

### Pattern 189: Node.js `worker_threads` `MessageChannel` scoped to test worker — isolating inter-thread communication state in tests  [official]

When testing code that uses `worker_threads` messaging, creating a fresh `MessageChannel` per test prevents message queues and port state from leaking between tests. Ports keep the event loop alive if not explicitly closed, causing `detectOpenHandles` and `detectAsyncLeaks` to report false-positive leaks.

```typescript
// tests/thread-bridge.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from '@jest/globals';
import { MessageChannel, MessagePort } from 'worker_threads';
import { ThreadBridge } from '../src/threadBridge';

describe('ThreadBridge message isolation', () => {
  let channel: MessageChannel;
  let bridge: ThreadBridge;
  let port1: MessagePort;
  let port2: MessagePort;

  beforeEach(() => {
    // Create a fresh channel per test — no message queue carryover
    channel = new MessageChannel();
    port1 = channel.port1;
    port2 = channel.port2;
    bridge = new ThreadBridge(port1);
    // Both ports must be active for messages to flow
    port1.start();
    port2.start();
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    // Close both ports — releases the event loop ref that causes open-handle warnings
    port1.close();
    port2.close();
  });

  test('sends a typed request and receives a response', async () => {
    const responsePromise = new Promise<{ result: number }>((resolve) => {
      port2.once('message', resolve);
    });

    bridge.send({ type: 'COMPUTE', payload: { a: 3, b: 4 } });

    // Simulate the "worker side" responding via port2
    port2.once('message', (msg: { type: string; payload: { a: number; b: number } }) => {
      port1.postMessage({ result: msg.payload.a + msg.payload.b });
    });

    const response = await responsePromise;
    expect(response.result).toBe(7);
  });

  test('does not receive messages from the previous test — channel is fresh', async () => {
    const received: unknown[] = [];
    port2.on('message', (m: unknown) => received.push(m));
    // No messages sent in this test — the queue from the previous test is gone
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
    expect(received).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use a per-test `MessageChannel` for any test of code that sends or listens to `MessagePort` events. Do NOT reuse a single shared channel across tests — unconsumed messages from one test will be delivered to the next test's listeners, corrupting assertions. Named alternative: use `worker_threads` `Worker` with `workerData` injection (Pattern 50) when the full worker subprocess isolation is needed, not just messaging isolation. [official]

---

### Pattern 190: MSW v2 `http.passthrough()` — selective real-network pass-through for hybrid isolation in mixed environments  [official]

MSW v2's `http.passthrough()` response allows specific requests to bypass the mock server and hit the real network, while all other requests remain intercepted. This enables hybrid isolation: third-party analytics, CDN assets, or internal health checks can reach real endpoints while the application API remains fully mocked.

```typescript
// tests/setup/msw-server.ts
import { setupServer } from 'msw/node';
import { http, HttpResponse, passthrough } from 'msw';

export const server = setupServer(
  // Allow health check calls to reach the real service (monitoring baseline)
  http.get('https://api.internal/health', () => passthrough()),

  // Allow CDN requests through — we never need to mock static assets
  http.get('https://cdn.example.com/*', () => passthrough()),

  // Mock the application API for complete isolation
  http.get('https://api.example.com/users', () =>
    HttpResponse.json([
      { id: '1', name: 'Alice' },
      { id: '2', name: 'Bob' },
    ])
  ),

  // Catch-all: block all other unmatched requests in CI
  // (prevents accidental real API calls)
  http.all('*', ({ request }) => {
    if (process.env.CI) {
      throw new Error(
        `Unexpected real network request in CI: ${request.method} ${request.url}`
      );
    }
    return passthrough(); // Allow locally for debugging
  })
);

// tests/user-list.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, beforeAll, afterEach, afterAll } from '@jest/globals';
import { server } from './setup/msw-server';
import { renderUserList } from '../src/userList';

beforeAll(() => server.listen({ onUnhandledRequest: 'error' }));
afterEach(() => server.resetHandlers());
afterAll(() => server.close());

describe('user list with hybrid MSW isolation', () => {
  test('renders mocked API users without hitting real network', async () => {
    const users = await renderUserList();
    expect(users).toEqual([{ id: '1', name: 'Alice' }, { id: '2', name: 'Bob' }]);
  });

  test('test-specific override replaces the default mock for this test only', async () => {
    server.use(
      http.get('https://api.example.com/users', () =>
        HttpResponse.json([{ id: '99', name: 'Charlie' }])
      )
    );
    const users = await renderUserList();
    expect(users).toEqual([{ id: '99', name: 'Charlie' }]);
    // resetHandlers() in afterEach restores the default mock after this test
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `passthrough()` for requests that must reach real endpoints (health checks, OAuth discovery, public CDN assets) to keep the real flow visible in integration tests. Do NOT use `passthrough()` for application API calls in unit or integration tests — every real network call is a test isolation violation that makes tests non-repeatable. Named alternative: `server.use(http.get(url, () => passthrough()))` added per-test for one-off pass-through without changing the base server setup. [official]

---

### Pattern 191: Playwright `test.describe.configure({ retries: N })` — suite-scoped retry budget for flaky E2E segments  [official]

`test.describe.configure({ retries: N })` scopes retry behaviour to a specific describe block rather than globally. This lets well-understood flaky segments (e.g., third-party SSO login flows) get a retry budget while the rest of the suite runs without retries, keeping overall CI signal quality high.

```typescript
// tests/auth/sso-flow.test.ts
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Only the SSO describe gets retries — because the IdP has unpredictable latency.
// The rest of the test suite runs without retries.
test.describe('SSO authentication flow', () => {
  test.describe.configure({ retries: 2 });

  test('redirects to IdP on unauthenticated access', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    // IdP redirect may be slow — retry budget handles transient IdP latency
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/sso\.idp\.example\.com\/login/, { timeout: 15_000 });
    await expect(page.getByLabel('Email')).toBeVisible();
  });

  test('completes SSO flow and lands on dashboard', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.click('[data-testid=sso-login-button]');
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/sso\.idp\.example\.com/);
    await page.fill('[name=email]', 'testuser@example.com');
    await page.fill('[name=password]', process.env.SSO_TEST_PASSWORD!);
    await page.click('[type=submit]');
    await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard', { timeout: 20_000 });
    await expect(page.getByText('Welcome, Test User')).toBeVisible();
  });
});

// This describe does NOT inherit retries — uses the playwright.config.ts default (0)
test.describe('local authentication flow', () => {
  test('logs in with local credentials without retries', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.fill('[name=email]', 'local@test.invalid');
    await page.fill('[name=password]', 'password123');
    await page.click('[type=submit]');
    await expect(page).toHaveURL('/dashboard');
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use suite-scoped retries to contain known-flaky third-party dependencies without polluting the global retry budget. Do NOT grant retries to tests that are flaky due to test isolation issues (shared state, timing bugs) — retries mask the real problem. Named alternative: `test.fixme(condition, reason)` when the flakiness is environment-specific and should be skipped in certain CI environments rather than retried. [official]

---

### Pattern 192: Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` with `leakWarningsTimeout` — tuning the async-handle grace period for legitimate long-lived resources  [official]

`detectAsyncLeaks: true` in Vitest reports open async handles after each test. The companion `leakWarningsTimeout` option (milliseconds) lets Vitest wait before classifying a handle as a leak, giving long-lived but correctly-managed resources time to close before the warning fires.

```typescript
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    detectAsyncLeaks: true,

    // Wait 500ms after a test completes before classifying open handles as leaks.
    // Increase for suites with slow I/O teardown (e.g., pg pool draining, TLS close_notify).
    // Default is 100ms — too low for real database teardown.
    leakWarningsTimeout: 500,

    pool: 'forks',
    poolOptions: {
      forks: {
        // Terminate forked processes that exceed this time after test completion
        // (backstop for cases where leakWarningsTimeout is not enough)
        execArgv: [],
      },
    },
  },
});

// tests/database-pool.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect } from 'vitest';
import { Pool } from 'pg';

describe('database connection pool — async leak detection', () => {
  test('pool ends cleanly within the leak warning timeout', async () => {
    const pool = new Pool({
      connectionString: process.env.TEST_DB_URL,
      max: 2,
      idleTimeoutMillis: 100, // connections close quickly after release
    });

    const client = await pool.connect();
    const { rows } = await client.query<{ now: Date }>('SELECT NOW() as now');
    client.release();

    // End the pool — this closes all idle connections
    await pool.end();

    expect(rows[0].now).toBeInstanceOf(Date);
    // pool.end() resolves before leakWarningsTimeout fires (500ms) — no leak warning
  });

  test('deliberately leaking pool triggers leak detection (negative test)', async () => {
    // This test demonstrates what a real leak looks like
    // Do NOT do this in production test code — this is for documentation only
    const pool = new Pool({ connectionString: process.env.TEST_DB_URL, max: 1 });
    const client = await pool.connect();
    await client.query('SELECT 1');
    // INTENTIONAL LEAK: client.release() and pool.end() are NOT called
    // detectAsyncLeaks will report this open handle after leakWarningsTimeout
    expect(client).toBeDefined();
    // Cleanup for the test suite's sake (not calling pool.end() to trigger the warning)
    client.release();
    await pool.end();
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `detectAsyncLeaks: true` with a `leakWarningsTimeout` tuned to your slowest legitimate teardown operation. Do NOT set `leakWarningsTimeout` too high (>2000ms) — a 2-second grace period per test multiplied across a 500-test suite adds 16 minutes of CI wait time. Named alternative: manually assert `pool.totalCount === 0` after teardown — more explicit than relying on leak detection but requires test code to know about the pool. [official]

---

### Pattern 193: Jest `sandboxInjectedGlobals` — injecting read-only globals into the VM sandbox for cross-test performance  [official]

`sandboxInjectedGlobals` lets you inject specific global references (like `Math`, `JSON`, `Intl`) directly into Jest's VM sandbox rather than re-creating them per test environment. This reduces per-test setup overhead for tests that reference heavy built-in objects frequently, while maintaining full isolation for mutable state.

```typescript
// jest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'jest';

export default defineConfig({
  testEnvironment: 'node',

  // Inject these built-ins directly into the VM sandbox as shared references.
  // They are read-only by design (no test can replace Math.random globally),
  // so sharing them does not introduce isolation risk.
  // This reduces garbage collection pressure from per-environment copies.
  sandboxInjectedGlobals: ['Math', 'JSON', 'Intl', 'console'],

  // Combine with restoreMocks to ensure console spies do not bleed between tests
  restoreMocks: true,
});

// tests/number-formatter.test.ts
import { describe, test, expect, jest } from '@jest/globals';
import { formatCurrency } from '../src/numberFormatter';

describe('formatCurrency — Intl.NumberFormat isolation', () => {
  test('formats USD amounts correctly', () => {
    // Intl is injected as a shared reference — no per-test construction overhead
    const result = formatCurrency(1234.56, 'USD', 'en-US');
    expect(result).toBe('$1,234.56');
  });

  test('formats EUR amounts with European locale', () => {
    const result = formatCurrency(1234.56, 'EUR', 'de-DE');
    // Intl.NumberFormat is shared — but formatCurrency creates its own formatter
    // internally, so locale is not shared state
    expect(result).toMatch(/1\.234,56/);
  });

  test('console.error from invalid currency does not bleed — restoreMocks clears spy', () => {
    // console is injected but jest.spyOn wraps it per test; restoreMocks cleans up
    const spy = jest.spyOn(console, 'error').mockImplementation(() => {});
    formatCurrency(-1, 'INVALID_CURRENCY', 'en-US');
    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalled();
    // spy is automatically restored after this test (restoreMocks: true)
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `sandboxInjectedGlobals` for immutable built-ins that all tests use and that have no shared mutable state. Do NOT inject globals that hold mutable state (e.g., custom singleton loggers, EventEmitter instances) — tests will share and corrupt that state. Named alternative: `globals: true` in Vitest makes all globals available without VM injection overhead, but it is a broader opt-in that also removes the isolation boundary between test files. [official]

---

### Pattern 194: Playwright `page.addInitScript` with typed `window` extension — type-safe global stub injection before page load  [official]

`page.addInitScript` runs a script before any page scripts execute. Combining it with a TypeScript `Window` interface extension gives type-safe access to injected stubs in `evaluate()` calls, while keeping the real page scripts isolated from test-controlled values.

```typescript
// tests/helpers/browserGlobals.ts
// Augment the Window interface so TypeScript knows about injected test globals
declare global {
  interface Window {
    __featureFlags: Record<string, boolean>;
    __mockUserId: string;
    __testMode: boolean;
  }
}

// tests/feature-flags.test.ts
import { test, expect, Page } from '@playwright/test';

async function injectTestGlobals(
  page: Page,
  flags: Record<string, boolean>,
  userId: string
): Promise<void> {
  // This script runs BEFORE the page's own scripts — overrides real feature flag init
  await page.addInitScript(
    ({ featureFlags, mockUserId }) => {
      window.__featureFlags = featureFlags;
      window.__mockUserId = mockUserId;
      window.__testMode = true;
    },
    { featureFlags: flags, mockUserId: userId }
  );
}

test('shows beta dashboard when beta flag is enabled', async ({ page }) => {
  // Inject BEFORE navigation — ensures the page reads these on first render
  await injectTestGlobals(page, { betaDashboard: true, legacyUI: false }, 'user-123');
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('beta-badge')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('legacy-ui-toggle')).not.toBeVisible();
});

test('shows legacy UI when legacyUI flag is enabled', async ({ page }) => {
  // Each test gets its own page — addInitScript is per-page, no bleed
  await injectTestGlobals(page, { betaDashboard: false, legacyUI: true }, 'user-456');
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  await expect(page.getByTestId('beta-badge')).not.toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('legacy-ui-toggle')).toBeVisible();
});

test('reads injected values from evaluate — type-safe', async ({ page }) => {
  await injectTestGlobals(page, { adminPanel: true }, 'admin-001');
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Type-safe access to __featureFlags via the Window augmentation
  const flags = await page.evaluate(() => window.__featureFlags);
  expect(flags.adminPanel).toBe(true);
  expect(flags.betaDashboard).toBeUndefined();
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use `addInitScript` with a typed `Window` extension for feature flag overrides, A/B test variant forcing, and authentication stub injection that must take effect before the first `DOMContentLoaded`. Do NOT use `addInitScript` to inject side-effectful code that makes real network calls — the injected code runs in the browser context and is not subject to MSW or `page.route()` interception. Named alternative: `page.route()` with `route.fulfill()` to override the API response that returns feature flags, which is more realistic but requires knowing the API contract. [official]

---

### Pattern 195: Vitest `test.extend` automatic fixture — cross-cutting isolation concerns without test-level boilerplate  [official]

An automatic fixture (`{ auto: true }`) runs for every test that uses the extended `test` object, regardless of whether the test explicitly requests it. This eliminates per-test boilerplate for cross-cutting isolation setup like resetting global singletons, clearing module-level caches, or enforcing invariant checks after each test.

```typescript
// fixtures/auto-isolation.ts
import { test as base, vi, expect } from 'vitest';
import { requestIdStore } from '../src/requestContext';
import { metricsRegistry } from '../src/metrics';
import { featureFlagCache } from '../src/featureFlags';

interface AutoIsolationFixtures {
  _autoIsolation: void; // phantom fixture — no test-visible value
}

export const test = base.extend<AutoIsolationFixtures>({
  _autoIsolation: [
    async ({}, use, taskContext) => {
      // PRE-TEST: Reset all global singletons before each test
      requestIdStore.disable();
      metricsRegistry.clear();
      featureFlagCache.invalidateAll();

      // Record the state before the test runs
      const initialFlagCount = featureFlagCache.size();

      await use(); // run the test

      // POST-TEST INVARIANT: Assert isolation was maintained
      // If a test added flags without cleaning up, this fails immediately
      const finalFlagCount = featureFlagCache.size();
      if (finalFlagCount !== initialFlagCount) {
        throw new Error(
          `Test "${taskContext.task.name}" leaked ${finalFlagCount - initialFlagCount} ` +
            `feature flag(s) into the cache without cleaning up.`
        );
      }
    },
    { auto: true }, // runs for every test — no opt-in required
  ],
});

// tests/feature-flag-service.test.ts
import { describe, expect } from 'vitest';
import { test } from '../fixtures/auto-isolation';
import { FeatureFlagService } from '../src/featureFlagService';

describe('FeatureFlagService', () => {
  test('evaluates a flag as disabled by default', async () => {
    // _autoIsolation runs automatically — no beforeEach needed
    const svc = new FeatureFlagService();
    expect(svc.isEnabled('new-checkout')).toBe(false);
  });

  test('evaluates an enabled flag correctly', async () => {
    const svc = new FeatureFlagService();
    svc.override('new-checkout', true);
    expect(svc.isEnabled('new-checkout')).toBe(true);
    // If override() writes to featureFlagCache without cleanup,
    // the auto-fixture's post-test invariant will catch it here.
  });
});
```

**Tradeoff:** Use automatic fixtures for cross-cutting isolation concerns that every test in a domain should enforce: singleton resets, cache invalidation, telemetry drain. Do NOT use `auto: true` for expensive setup (e.g., Docker container lifecycle) — every test pays the cost whether it needs it or not. Named alternative: a shared `beforeEach` in a `describe` block achieves the same reset without fixtures, but does not enforce the post-test invariant check that automatic fixtures can provide. [official]

---

## Real-World Gotchas — Cycle 31

200. **Vitest `test.override` does NOT work inside `test.extend()` fixture initialisation — overrides are applied at the suite level, not propagated into fixture setup closures, so the fixture always sees its default value.** [community]
    WHY: `test.override({ timeout: 60_000 })` replaces the fixture value in the test function's argument, but the fixture's own `async ({}, use)` setup code runs with the base fixture parameters, not the overridden ones. A fixture that reads `timeout` during its initialisation (e.g., to set `pool.query` statement timeout) will always receive the unoverridden default. The workaround is to pass the override value through a separate fixture whose value is set explicitly, or to read the overridden value inside the test body and pass it to the service rather than inside the fixture.

201. **Jest `globalsCleanup: 'on'` wipes `globalThis` references set by `jest.globalSetup` — setup data is gone before the first test file runs when a `testEnvironment` creates the VM context fresh.** [community]
    WHY: `jest.globalSetup` runs in a Node.js subprocess outside any VM context. Values written to `globalThis` in `globalSetup` are in the host process's global scope. When `testEnvironment: 'node'` creates a new VM context for the first test file, `globalsCleanup: 'on'` resets that context's `globalThis` before any tests run, wiping any globals that were "copied" into it. The fix is to use `protectProperties` (Pattern 186) or store setup data in a temp file / environment variable, not in `globalThis`.

202. **Playwright `page.clock.install` does not freeze `performance.timeOrigin` — code that computes elapsed time by subtracting `performance.timeOrigin` from `performance.now()` sees a real origin even when `now()` is faked.** [community]
    WHY: `page.clock.install` replaces `performance.now()` with the fake clock's value but leaves `performance.timeOrigin` pointing to the real timestamp when the page loaded. Any elapsed-time calculation using `performance.now() - performance.timeOrigin` will produce a large real number, not the expected small fake-clock delta. Fix: either avoid `performance.timeOrigin` in production code (prefer `Date.now()` which IS fully faked), or assert on absolute `performance.now()` values, not relative elapsed times.

203. **Vitest `detectAsyncLeaks` false-positive for Prisma `$disconnect()` — Prisma's connection pool runs a background keepalive ping that fires during the leak-grace-window even after `$disconnect()` resolves.** [community]
    WHY: `prisma.$disconnect()` closes the connection pool and resolves the Promise, but the underlying `@prisma/driver-adapter` internally schedules one final cleanup microtask for its TCP socket `FIN_WAIT` handling. Vitest's `detectAsyncLeaks` samples open handles immediately after the test's teardown resolves, catching this microtask in flight. The warning reads "detected open TCP socket" even though teardown was correct. Fix: increase `leakWarningsTimeout` to 300ms to give the Prisma socket time to close, or suppress the warning for the Prisma client using Vitest's `openHandlesTimeout` option.

204. **MSW `passthrough()` in Node.js does NOT propagate `fetch` headers modified by the intercept handler — the original request headers are forwarded to the real network, not any mutations made before calling `passthrough()`.** [community]
    WHY: `passthrough()` is a response factory that tells MSW to let the request through unmodified. Unlike `route.continue({ headers: {...} })` in Playwright, MSW `passthrough()` does not accept a modified request argument. Headers added with `request.headers.set()` before returning `passthrough()` are discarded. If you need to forward a modified request (e.g., injecting a correlation ID before passthrough), you must use `fetch(request)` manually and return an `HttpResponse` from the result instead.

205. **Playwright `test.describe.configure({ retries: 2 })` resets the retry counter for EACH test independently — a test that passes on retry 1 does not "use up" retries for sibling tests in the describe block.** [community]
    WHY: The retry budget `N` is a per-test limit, not a shared describe-level budget. In a describe with 10 tests and `retries: 2`, every single test can fail and be retried up to 2 times — the total potential CI runtime is 30 test executions (10 × 3 max). Teams sometimes configure `retries: 2` expecting it to mean "the suite gets 2 total extra attempts" and are surprised by CI jobs taking 3× longer. Fix: document the per-test nature of retries, set `retries: 1` as a conservative ceiling, and treat any consistently retrying test as a priority fix.

206. **Jest `maxConcurrency` applies per-worker, not globally — with `maxWorkers: 4` and `maxConcurrency: 5`, up to 20 concurrent `test.concurrent` tests can run simultaneously across all workers.** [community]
    WHY: `maxConcurrency` limits concurrency within a single worker. Each of 4 workers can run 5 concurrent tests, producing 20 simultaneous executions. Database connection pools sized to `maxConcurrency` (5) will be exhausted immediately because all 4 workers compete for the same pool. Fix: size external resource pools to `maxWorkers × maxConcurrency`, or reduce `maxWorkers` to 1 when using `test.concurrent` with a shared resource that has strict connection limits.

207. **Node.js `MessageChannel` `port.close()` emits `'close'` synchronously but pending `'message'` events already in the queue are discarded silently — teardown calling `port.close()` before all sent messages are processed produces silent message loss.** [community]
    WHY: `port.close()` terminates the port immediately. Any `postMessage()` calls made before `close()` that have not yet been delivered via the microtask queue are dropped without error. A test that calls `port.close()` in `afterEach` while a deferred `postMessage` is still in flight will silently lose the message, making the next test receive an empty queue and potentially pass with missing assertions. Fix: drain the port's pending messages (listen until a sentinel message arrives) before calling `close()`, or use `port.unref()` only when you are sure the queue is empty.

208. **Vitest automatic fixtures with `{ auto: true }` run in every test including those that use `test.skip` or `test.todo` — the fixture's setup and teardown code executes even for tests the developer expects to be completely bypassed.** [community]
    WHY: Vitest runs automatic fixtures as part of the test lifecycle infrastructure, not as user-visible test logic. A skipped test still triggers the fixture's `use()` call (though the test body does not run). If the auto fixture's setup performs side effects (creates a temp directory, inserts a database row), those side effects occur for every skipped test. Fix: check `taskContext.task.mode` inside the auto fixture and short-circuit setup for `'skip'` and `'todo'` modes using an early `await use()` call before the side-effectful setup code.

209. **Jest `globalsCleanup: 'on'` silently passes when a global is set via `Object.defineProperty` with `configurable: false` — the cleanup cannot delete non-configurable properties and skips them without warning.** [community]
    WHY: Jest's `globalsCleanup` mechanism iterates known added properties and calls `delete globalThis[key]`. If the property was defined as `configurable: false` (e.g., by a polyfill or third-party setup file that uses `Object.defineProperty`), the delete silently fails — the property remains on `globalThis` for subsequent test files despite `'on'` being set. The leak is invisible in Jest output. Fix: audit setup files for `Object.defineProperty` calls with `configurable: false`; replace with plain assignment, or use `protectProperties` intentionally rather than accidentally.

210. **Playwright `page.addInitScript` called multiple times accumulates scripts — each navigation re-runs ALL scripts registered on the page, not just the most recent one.** [community]
    WHY: `page.addInitScript` appends to an internal list of init scripts. If a test helper calls `addInitScript` once, and then a nested fixture calls it again for a different purpose, both scripts run on every subsequent `page.goto()`. In tests that navigate multiple times, earlier scripts run repeatedly, which can re-set flags that a later test phase intentionally changed. Fix: use `browserContext.addInitScript` instead if the script should persist for the whole context, or structure tests to navigate once per page instance and avoid repeated `addInitScript` calls within a single test.

---

## Quick Reference — Cycle 31

| Problem | Symptom | Solution | Framework |
|---------|---------|----------|-----------|
| `globalThis` global wiped by `globalsCleanup: 'on'` | Setup data gone before first test | Use `protectProperties` from `jest-util` | Jest |
| `test.override` value not seen in fixture setup | Fixture uses default despite override | Pass override through test body, not fixture init | Vitest |
| `page.clock.install` does not fake `performance.timeOrigin` | Elapsed-time calculation huge/wrong | Assert absolute `performance.now()`, avoid `timeOrigin` difference | Playwright |
| Prisma `$disconnect` triggers `detectAsyncLeaks` warning | False-positive open TCP socket | Increase `leakWarningsTimeout` to ≥300ms | Vitest |
| MSW `passthrough()` drops header mutations | Modified headers not forwarded | Use manual `fetch(request)` + `HttpResponse` instead of `passthrough()` | MSW v2 |
| `test.describe.configure({ retries })` uses 3× CI time | All 10 tests each retry 2× | Set `retries: 1` max; treat retry as fix signal | Playwright |
| `maxConcurrency` + `maxWorkers` exhausts DB pool | Connection refused errors | Size pool to `maxWorkers × maxConcurrency` | Jest |
| `port.close()` in `afterEach` drops pending messages | Silent message loss; next test empty | Drain port queue before close | Node.js |
| Auto fixture setup runs for `test.skip` tests | Unintended side effects on skipped tests | Check `taskContext.task.mode` and short-circuit | Vitest |
| `globalsCleanup: 'on'` misses `configurable: false` globals | Non-configurable property persists silently | Replace `Object.defineProperty` with plain assignment | Jest |
| `addInitScript` accumulates across multiple calls | Old scripts re-run on subsequent navigations | Use `browserContext.addInitScript` or single-navigation test structure | Playwright |
| Suite-level `aroundAll` teardown skipped on worker crash | Seeded data persists, next run polluted | Add DB-level cleanup in globalTeardown as backstop | Vitest |

| Playwright `page.clock` | Official | https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-clock | `install` before goto; `fastForward`; `performance.timeOrigin` caveat |
| Playwright `describe.configure` | Official | https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-describe-configure | Suite-scoped `retries`, `timeout`, `mode` — per-describe, not global |
| MSW `passthrough()` | Official | https://mswjs.io/docs/api/passthrough | Selective real-network pass-through; header mutation limitation |

| Martin Fowler Non-Determinism | Community | https://martinfowler.com/articles/nonDeterminism.html | Quarantine taxonomy; pool-size-1 technique; rebuild-not-clean principle |
